euhgul1: Sexes alike in plumage; males larger, bulkier-billed, flatter-fronted. Adult breeding: light grey mantle and upperwings; head, neck, underparts, rump and tail white; black wingtips with white mirrors. Non-breeding: brown streaking on head and neck. Juvenile and first-winter brown with darker streaks; second-winter whiter-headed with grey back; third-winter near-adult but brown in the wing; adult at four years. Bill yellow, red gonys spot confined to the lower mandible; iris sulphur-yellow, orbital ring yellow, orange or red; legs flesh-pink, yellowish in some Baltic birds.
gretit1: Male: crown, nape, throat and bib glossy blue-black; cheeks and ear-coverts pure white, cleanly framed by black; breast lemon-yellow split by a broad black mid-line from bib to vent, widening between the legs. Mantle olive-green, wings blue-grey with one white bar, tail blue-grey with white outer tips. Female: duller, stripe narrower, sometimes broken. Juvenile: nape olive-brown, rump grey. Bill blackish horn with paler edges; iris bright reddish-brown to blackish-brown; legs and feet blue-grey to slate.
mutswa: Adult wholly white. Juvenile grey-brown-white, moulting into white plumage during the first summer or the second autumn. A rare recessive morph, the 'Polish swan', has white downy young and grey or pink feet as an adult. Bill orange with black nail, base and knob; a black wedge runs from the bill base to the hazel eye; legs black-grey.
comcuc: Male slate-grey above; chin, throat and upper breast pale grey, cut off sharply from white underparts broadly barred grey-brown; tail dark slate-grey, white-tipped. Female grey morph: as male but breast washed pinkish-buff and finely barred. Rufous morph, mostly females: upperparts reddish-brown with black bars narrower than the rufous ones. Juvenile: variable, chestnut-brown and heavily barred or plain grey, feathers whitish-edged. Iris, orbital ring, bill-base and feet yellow. Outer toe reversible, as in all cuckoos.
laplon: Male: crown, cheeks, throat and upper breast black; white supercilium behind the black ear-coverts; nape chestnut; back streaked black and white; median coverts white-tipped; underparts white, flanks black-spotted. Female: no black on head or throat, white throat patch under a grey collar, buff supercilium, black comma on the cheek. Other plumages plainer, orange-brown head, chestnut nape and wing panels. Bill thick, straw-yellow with a black tip, paler yellow in the female; legs dark.
gyrfal: Polymorphic: white, silver, brown and black morphs. Grey birds grey to grey-brown above with ash-grey barring, white below finely spotted, flanks and trousers barred. Brown morph cream-streaked on crown and nape. Juvenile: cold dark brown-grey above, coarsely streaked below. Northern birds paler; Greenland birds white with dark spots. Cere and feet yellow in adults, blue-grey in juveniles; iris dark brown in a yellow eye-ring; bill blue-grey with a darker tip.
blutit: White forehead into a pale blue crown; narrow black eyestripe to a dark blue nape band, set off by a white line; white cheeks bounded by a black chin-spot and black-blue collar. Back dull green, rump grey-blue, wings and tail blue, one white bar; underparts bright yellow with a dark line down the belly. Juvenile: cheeks and supercilium yellow, duller. Bill dark horn-brown; iris brown; feet dark blue-grey, claws grey.
eurwig: Male: chestnut head with creamy-buff forehead blaze, pink-grey breast, vermiculated grey back and flanks, black stern, white belly, brilliant white forewing patch and dark green speculum. Female: brown head, vermiculated grey-brown back, rusty breast and flanks, white belly, upperwing grey with no white. Eclipse male female-like; juvenile as female. Bill small, pale grey-blue with black nail and black lower edge; male's tip black.
comsni: Body mottled brown with straw-yellow stripes above, pale below, belly extensively white. Head striped: dark crown split by a buff central stripe, dark eye-stripe with pale stripes above and below, dark lores broadening towards the bill-base. Neck and breast streaked yellowish-brown, coarsening to V-shaped zigzags on breast sides and flanks. Sexes alike. Legs short, stout, greenish-grey to yellowish-green; bill reddish-brown at base, dark brown at tip; iris brown.
whteag: Adult mostly brown, with head, neck, upper breast and upper back paler yellowish-ochre; tail short, wedge-shaped and white. Juvenile: dark brown throughout with a dark tail, growing whiter with each moult and fully adult at five years. Bill very heavy and yellow, heavier than Golden Eagle's; cere and iris pale yellow; talons large and pale yellow; tarsi unfeathered to the toes.
norful: Grey and white: head, neck and underparts white or dark grey; upperwing grey-blue; rump and tail paler grey; pale inner primaries on the upperwing; no black wingtips, unlike gulls. Light, dark ('blue') and intermediate morphs; only the dark morph is more than dark-edged below. Dark eye set in a grey loral smudge. Bill short and thick, mostly yellowish, darkening towards the nostrils and often mottled black there; legs bluish to yellowish-green.
greshe: Dark brown above with a white nape band and a white horseshoe of uppertail-coverts; blackish-brown cap sharply cut from the white underparts; dark neck-side patch. Underwing white, dark-edged, with dark marks on the secondary coverts; dingy dark belly patch and undertail-coverts. Moult in July–August gives white bars across the upperwing. Juvenile greyer, paler-fringed. Bill black and relatively slender; feet pink.
gbbgul: Adult greyish-black mantle and upperwings — no other very large black-backed gull in the North Atlantic — with bold white mirrors and a white trailing edge; head, neck, underparts, rump and tail white. Juvenile boldly black-and-white chequered, not the dusky grey of Herring Gull; whitish head finely barred, white rump lightly spotted, narrow dark tail-band. Adult at four years. Bill pale yellow with a red gonys spot; iris pale yellow to amber, orbital ring red or orange; legs grey-pink in all plumages.
eurbla: Male uniformly black, faintly grey- or bronze-fringed below in good light; flight feathers bleached by spring. Female dark olive-brown to olive-grey above with paler forehead, weak supercilium and dark lores, throat pale grey and streaked, breast brown-grey to rufous, dark-spotted. Juvenile like the female but pale-spotted above; first-year male black with a brown folded wing. Male bill orange-yellow, darkening in late summer, with bright orange-yellow orbital ring; iris dark brown. Female bill pale horn-yellow, dark-ridged; eye-ring weak. Legs dark brown.
norgan: Adult white with dark brown to black primaries, primary coverts and alulae; head and neck washed buff-yellow, strongest when breeding and deeper in males, occasionally absent altogether. Bare black lores and chin give the hard-faced look. Fledglings look white-spotted from pale feather tips; juveniles dark grey-brown speckled, whitening over four to five years into adult plumage. Bill blue-grey with dark edges and a black groove running back to the eye; iris pale blue-grey; bare black facial skin, cobalt orbital ring.
sposta1: Dark, oily-looking black, faintly purple- or green-glossed in bright light; wholly unspotted in spring and summer, in winter only very small pale spots from pale feather tips. Females and first-summer males show pale spots on the undertail-coverts; winter and first-winter females are spotted on back, belly and undertail-coverts, crown usually unspotted. Juvenile dull brown, darker than a young Common Starling. Bill yellow in summer, blue-based in males and pink-based in females, blackish and duller in winter. Legs bright pink; juvenile bill black, legs brown.
bklkit: Adult white on head, body, underwing and tail; back and upperwing grey in two tones with the outer three primaries solid black and without white tips, so the wing looks three-toned at distance. Winter: dark grey smudge behind the eye and a grey hind-neck collar. Juvenile and first-winter show a dark ear-crescent. Bill plain greenish-yellow, dusky-olive in winter, blackish-grey in juveniles; legs black, occasionally pinkish-grey to reddish; gape and orbital ring bright red; iris dark.
commur: Breeding adult black-brown on head, back, tail and upperwing, white below and on the underwing-coverts; nominate birds black, albionis dark brown, most obviously in southern Britain. Winter: face and chin white with a dark spur running back from the eye, flanks often dark-streaked. 'Bridled' birds show a white eye-ring and a white line back across the cheek. Bill and legs dark grey; the grey-black feet stand out against the body in flight.
manshe: Slate-black above, pure white below. Head and neck sides mottled grey-and-white but sharply demarcated — white bristly feathers cut a crescent between ear-coverts and hind-neck; white bulge behind the wing on the rump. Underwing mostly white with a broad dark grey trailing edge, widest at the tip, a narrow dark leading edge, and often a dark axillary bar. Bill dark brown-grey to blackish, often paler at the base; iris blackish; legs and feet pink or bluish flesh, dark brown along the outer edges.
sooshe: All dark: looks wholly black in poor light; in good light dark chocolate-brown to dark grey, with a silvery strip along the centre of the underwing.
redwin: Sexes alike: plain brown above, white underparts streaked and spotted dark brown, belly almost wholly white. Best marks the creamy-white supercilium and the rusty-red flanks and underwing-coverts — the red shows in flight and still on the flanks of perched birds. Subspecies coburni darker overall and rather larger.
y00743: Black with a green or purple sheen, much greener than a Rook's gloss. Two morphs: wholly black birds in western Europe and eastern Asia, black-and-grey birds between — black head, chin, upper breast, flight feathers, some coverts and tail, ash-grey elsewhere; intermediates occur. Juvenile browner and duller. Bill, legs and feet black; iris dark brown. Juvenile iris blue to greyish, gape red at first.
corshe1: Brownish-grey upperparts, the hand usually darker; head pale grey with no sharp cap; underparts white. Lacks the brown belly patch, dark shoulder markings and black cap of Great Shearwater. No white tongues on the undersides of the outer three primaries. Bill proportionately large, pale yellow with a black band near the tip — the pale bill is often visible at very long range.
rinphe1: Male: body barred bright gold to fiery copper-red and chestnut, glossed green and purple, rump sometimes blue; wing coverts white or cream; head bottle-green with a small crest, elongated nape feathers forming ear-tufts, and bare scarlet face wattles. Nominate colchicus and some other races lack the white neck ring. Female and juvenile dull mottled brown throughout. Bill greenish horn in males, dark brownish horn in females; iris pale orange in males, orange to amber in females; legs unfeathered, male spurred.
litshe1: Dark above, pale below; face pale with a darkly contrasting eye — the white cheek reaching up over the eye; silvery panel in the upperwing, and at close range clearly white covert tips above. Feet blue.
cowpig1: Mostly grey, paler over the back, with blue-green gloss on head and neck; breast pinkish, paling to grey below. Neck sides carry a green band, a white patch and a glossy purple-red band; broad white wing-bars show in flight; tail and wings boldly marked black. Juvenile lacks the white neck patches until six to eight months old. Adult bill yellow with reddish cere, iris pale yellow to orange; juvenile bill, cere and eye grey. Legs short, stout and brownish-pink.
gresku1: Adult streaked greyish-brown with rusty-buff shaft-streaks above and a black cap; underparts dull grey-toned; wings blackish-brown with a bold white flash; tail black-brown. Juvenile warmer brown and unstreaked below. Bill and feet almost black.
houspa: Male: lead-grey crown flanked by chestnut from eye to hind neck; cheeks pale grey to whitish; black bib from bill over throat to upper breast, veiled by pale fringes in autumn and clean only by spring; back brown, black-streaked; one clear white wing-bar; underparts ash-grey. Female plain grey-brown, finely marked, pale supercilium strongest behind the eye; no chestnut, no bib.
eurrob1: Sexes alike. Orange-red forehead, throat and breast, spreading onto head and neck sides and edged bluish-grey along neck and breast. Upperparts olive-brown, greyer by spring through wear; flanks grey to olive-brown, belly greyish-white, undertail-coverts cream. Coverts tipped rusty, giving a thin buff wing-bar, clearest on juveniles. Juvenile brown above with yellow mottling, red appearing gradually on the breast. Bill black to blackish-grey and pointed, with three or four rictal bristles each side; iris and legs dark brown.
eurjac: Shiny black; purple or blue sheen to crown, forehead and secondaries, green-blue to throat, primaries and tail; cheeks, nape and neck light grey to silvery-grey; underparts slate-grey. Sexes alike. Juvenile: duller and less sharply demarcated, head sooty black, neck sides dark grey, underparts greyish to sooty black. Bill short, stout, black, about 75% the length of the rest of the head; legs black; adult iris greyish to silvery-white, juvenile light blue.
medgul1: Breeding adult white with very pale grey mantle and wings and pure white primaries, no black tips; black hood reaching the nape, bold white eye-crescents. Non-breeding: hood reduced to a dusky bandit mask through the eye with grey streaking on the hindcrown. Juvenile: scaly mantle, brown secondaries, grey scapulars, blackish-brown primaries and tail-tip, white below. Bill short but stout, dark red with a black subterminal band and yellow to orange tip; legs dark red. Juvenile: bill grey-pink, dark-tipped; legs slate-grey.
wispet: Essentially dark brown in all plumages but for a broad white rump reaching well down the sides, and white flanks; diffuse pale band along the upper wing-coverts; underwing uniformly dark with a faint bronze gloss, lacking any white lining. Sexes alike. Toe webbing yellow, spotted black in pre-breeding birds.
sabgul: Striking tricoloured wing: pale grey back and coverts, four black outer primaries, white inner primaries and secondaries, forming a broad white triangle. Breeding adult hood slate-grey, cut off from the white neck by a narrow black collar; winter head white with dark grey nape. Juvenile: grey replaced by brown, black terminal tail band, grey-brown head running down the breast-sides. Bill black with a yellow tip, about 2.5 cm long; legs grey.
bripet: All black, greyer at the colony and browner when worn, except a snow-white rump extending onto the sides of the tail base and a broad white band along the underwing; undertail-coverts black. Fresh juveniles may show a narrow white bar on the upperwing. Sexes alike.
balshe1: Upperparts greyish-brown, underparts dirty white with a grey-brown wash thickening from the lower belly to the undertail-coverts; flanks never pure white, the border with the upperparts diffuse; centre of underwing diffusely ash-grey to off-white with a brown bar in the axillaries, the underwing looking dark. Juvenile as adult, told June–September by fresh upperpart feathering while adults moult.
parjae: Three morphs. Light morph: brown back, mainly white underparts, black cap, yellowish-white head and neck sides; dark morph uniformly dark brown; intermediates dark with paler underparts, head and neck. All morphs show a white flash in the black primaries, seen from below as a white wedge. Juvenile: warm brown, sandy to rufous or dark brown. Bill bluish at the base, black at the tip; legs black in adults, blue-grey in juveniles.
whiwag: Black, white and grey throughout. Male: white forehead, face and neck sides; rear crown, nape, chin, throat and upper breast glossy black, sharply cut against the white face and grey back; rump slate-grey; underparts and undertail-coverts white; two white wingbars; tail black with broad white outer edges, striking as the bird flies up. Juvenile: duller and more diffuse. Bill, legs and feet black; bill with a horn-coloured base in non-breeding plumage.
fieldf: Slate to ash-grey head, nape, hind neck, lower back and rump; mantle and scapulars dark chestnut-brown; tail blackish-grey. Whitish supercilium, black lores. Chin, throat and upper breast ochre-buff with bold blackish streaks; flanks with dark arrowhead spots; belly, undertail-coverts and underwing-coverts white. Sexes alike. First-winter: white tips to the upper wing-coverts. Bill yellow to yellow-orange with a dark tip; legs dark brown to dark grey; iris dark brown.
doveki: Breeding: head, neck, upper breast, back and upperwing black; underparts and undertail-coverts white; underwing grey; white trailing edge to the secondaries and white fringes to the scapulars. Winter: throat, fore-neck, breast and sides of head white up to the black cheeks. Sexes alike; first-winter often brownish. Bill and iris black in all plumages; most birds show a small but distinct white eye-spot; feet grey and webbed.
combuz1: Highly variable, from almost white to almost black-brown; most European birds dark brown above and on head and mantle. Tail grey-brown to rust with eight to twelve narrow dark bars, a pale tip and a broad dark subterminal band. Breast-patch usually dark-streaked; underwing usually paler than the body; primary tips always dark. Juvenile breast band streaked, adult barred. Iris dark brown to almost yellow.
scoshe1: Upperparts brownish-grey, feathers pale-fringed, hand darker; head pale grey without contrast beyond a dark eye-patch; upper tail-coverts whitish-tipped, a variable pale band before the dark tail. Underparts white, breast-sides grey; underwing and undertail framed by clear dark edges, with a pale bar from elbow to carpal; more white on the outer primaries than Cory's, especially P10. Bill proportionally large, pale yellow with a dark band near the tip, visible at long range; legs and feet pale flesh.
jacsni: Mottled brown above with yellow back stripes showing in flight, pale below. Crown glossy blackish-brown, no central crown-stripe: two pale lateral crown-stripes separated from the broad pale yellow supercilium by dark. Black eyestripe broad before the eye, narrower behind, ending in a dark ear-covert patch. Neck, breast and fore-flanks washed brown with heavy dark streaks; belly and undertail white.
barpet: Very dark throughout — sooty black above, sootier brown below — but for a square white rump patch, broader than long, and a few pale feathers on flanks and undertail-coverts; upperwing-coverts slightly paler, the bar diffuse and not sharply marked.
comcha: Male: black forehead, blue-grey crown, nape and upper mantle, browner-grey in winter; lower mantle and scapulars a brown saddle; rump light olive-green; face, throat and breast dull rust-red fading to creamy-pink on the belly. Female: olive-grey above, paler below. Juvenile like female. Both sexes: white shoulder patch, white wingbar and white wedges in the outer tail feathers. Iris dark brown; legs grey-brown. Male's bill bluish-grey with a small black tip in spring, pale grey in winter; female's horn-brown year-round.
mallar3: Male: glossy bottle-green head, narrow white collar, purple-tinged chestnut breast, pale grey belly, grey-brown wings; black stern with curled black upper tail-coverts, outer tail feathers beige-white. Both sexes: iridescent purple-blue speculum with black then broad white border. Female: mottled buff to dark brown, buff cheeks, supercilium, throat and neck, darker crown and eye-stripe. Juvenile: as female. Male's bill plain dull yellow to yellowish-orange, black-tipped; female's orange with dark grey ridge, or mottled brown; legs yellow to yellow-red.
comkin1: Male ispida: crown, nape, wing-coverts and tail green-blue with azure barring on the head feathers; back and rump brilliant pale azure to cobalt; rufous patch by the bill base and rufous ear-coverts; blue-green malar stripe; sharp white neck blaze and white throat; underparts warm rufous-chestnut. Juvenile: duller, greener above, paler below. Male's bill all black; female's lower mandible orange-red at the base. Legs and feet bright red; juvenile bill black, feet grey.
sonthr1: Sexes alike. Plain brown above, colder in tone eastwards; faint pale supercilium, clearest over the forehead. Below cream to yellow-buff, paler on the belly, neatly spotted blackish — narrow streaks on chin and throat massing into a malar stripe, spots larger and rounder towards the belly. Underwing grey with warm rusty-yellow coverts. Juvenile: buff-orange streaks on back and wing-coverts. Bill yellowish; legs and feet pink.
winwre4: Rufous-brown above, greyer buff-white below; fine dark barring throughout, on wings, tail and flanks too; indistinct cream supercilium ending at dark ear-coverts; dark lores; primaries dark brown with pale spots on the outer webs. Sexes alike. Juvenile: barring weaker, underparts mottled. Bill blackish-brown above, yellowish below; iris nut-brown; legs pale brown to orange-brown or flesh.
lbbgul: Adult breeding: head, neck, breast, belly, underwing, rump and tail pure white; upperparts slate-grey to velvety black-grey by race; outer primaries black, contrasting little on the darkest birds; narrow white trailing edge running unbroken to the fifth primary; small white mirrors. Winter: head grey-streaked. Juvenile: vermiculated black, white, grey and buff, all primaries wholly dark. Bill yellow with a red gonys spot; legs yellow.
hoocro1: Ash-grey body, dark feather shafts giving a streaked look; head, throat, upper breast, wings, tail and thigh feathers black and mostly glossy; black bib ragged and variable; black on the wing takes in the flight feathers, primary coverts and greater coverts. Newly hatched young much blacker; juvenile duller. Bill and legs black; iris dark brown. Juvenile: iris blue-grey, gape red at first.
eurgol1: Red face-mask, black crown and nape, white head-sides; back pale warm brown, rump white; underparts white with buff-brown breast patches and flanks; wings black with a broad bright yellow band; tail black, white spots in the outer third. Female: mask smaller, not past the eye, lesser coverts brown not black. Juvenile: head plain, back greyer, yellow wing-band still obvious. Bill ivory, long and pointed; pure white when breeding, otherwise with a grey or black mark at the tip.
commoo3: Dark overall: upperparts dark olive-brown, head, neck and underparts dark slate-grey to blackish; broad white streaks along the flanks; undertail-coverts white with a black centre. Juvenile: grey-brown above, grey-white below, chin and throat dirty white, neck-sides faintly rusty, no red shield. Bill red with yellow tip; frontal shield red, rounded top, parallel sides, reaching well up; iris red; legs yellow-green, red band above the joint.
dunnoc1: Crown, supercilium, nape, throat and breast lead- to slate-grey; back and wings rich dark brown streaked black; underparts brownish and plain. Sexes alike, male averaging a little more grey on head and neck. Juvenile: head browner, feathering loose and fluffy, streaking heavier and reaching the throat and breast. Bill dark and thin; legs red-brown.
meapip1: Brown above with an olive to grey-green cast and marked dark back-streaking, buff below; darker barring over most of the plumage, breast finely streaked and little yellow on it; supercilium whitish; tail brown with narrow white outer edges. Legs pale pinkish-yellow to reddish.
razorb: Breeding: head, neck, back and feet black, breast and belly white, underwing and axillaries wholly white; thin white line from eye to bill; bill grooved near the tip and crossed by a bold white stripe. Non-breeding: chin, cheeks, face behind eye and neck-sides white, head and bill lines faint or gone. Juvenile: as winter adult, bill shorter, narrower, plain black. Bill black, deep and blunt, grooved and white-striped near the tip, slimmer with fainter grooves in winter; feet black.
eurbul: Male: crown, face and chin black, wings and tail black glossed blue, back blue-grey, rump and undertail white, broad white wing-bar; cheeks, breast, flanks and upper belly bright rose-red. Female: back brown-grey, underparts pale grey-brown with a faint reddish-lilac cast. Juvenile: browner still, head pale with no black cap, bill without black. Bill short, thick, black; iris deep brown; feet black-brown, blackish in the female.
whoswa: Adult pure white, head and neck often stained rusty-yellow where the water is rich in tannin or iron. Juvenile: uniform pale grey to grey-brown, paler and plainer than a young Mute Swan, bill pattern as the adult's but pink for the yellow and blackish-grey for the black; whitens through the first and second year. Bill 9–12 cm, black with yellow cere and base, the yellow reaching below the nostril and exceeding the black; iris dark brown; eyes small.
rook1: Black throughout with a blue to purple sheen, faintly reddish in some lights, crown and nape flashing green or violet; head, neck and shoulder feathers dense and silky with no visible shafts; thigh feathering shaggy and lax. Juvenile: black with a faint green gloss, hindneck, back and underparts brown-black, face still feathered. Bill grey-black, pointed, its base bare, scurfy and whitish to pale yellow in adults from February–May of the second year; legs black; iris dark brown.
euroys1: Head, breast and upperparts black, underparts white, lower back white, tail white with a broad black terminal band; in winter the black is duller and a white throat collar shows, briefly in adults, longer in immatures. Juvenile: mantle browner with pale washed feather edges, white collar, whitish flecks on throat and neck-sides. Bill orange-red to red, dark-tipped in juveniles and first-summer birds; legs pink, matt grey-pink in juveniles; eyes red.
wlwwar: Greenish-brown to olive-green above, crown and mantle olive; off-white to yellowish below, throat and breast pale green-yellow, belly and vent white to yellow-white; strong pale yellow supercilium, longest and clearest behind the eye; wings plain, no wing-bars. Juvenile: yellower below. Sexes alike. Legs pale pinkish-yellow to brown-pink; bill pale, fine and pointed.
corbun1: Lark-like and drab, with no showy head pattern: grey-brown to mid-brown above, forward back and scapulars boldly streaked black-brown, hind back and rump more weakly so; underparts whitish to grey-buff, streaked on breast and flanks, the streaks gathering into a gorget round the throat; lesser coverts dark and white-tipped; tail plain brown. Bill heavy and conical, mandibles yellowish-pink at the sides; eye conspicuously dark.
grswoo: Glossy blue-black above with a large white oval shoulder patch each side; face and neck-sides white; black malar stripe and a black line from shoulder to nape reaching half across the breast; flight feathers and tail barred black and white; underparts white with scarlet lower belly and vent. Male: crimson nape patch. Female: none. Juvenile: red crown, belly pink. Bill slate-black; legs greenish-grey; eye deep red.
barswa: Upperparts glossy steel blue-black; forehead, chin and throat chestnut-red, cut off from the off-white underparts by a broad dark blue breast band; wing and tail feathers black, a line of white spots across the outer tail. Female: streamers shorter, blue duller, underparts paler, less rufous on throat and forehead. Juvenile: browner, face pale rufous, underparts whiter, no streamers.
cangoo: Head and neck black with a broad white chinstrap running from the throat up behind the eye; black neck cut sharply against a pale grey breast; upperparts grey-brown to red-brown by race; flanks and belly beige-brown, clearly barred; vent and uppertail-coverts white, tail black-grey. Sexes alike. Odd birds show dark cheeks, white foreheads or white necks. Bill and feet black to grey-black; iris dark brown.
ivogul: Adult wholly pure white, without the grey saddle of other gulls. Juvenile and first-winter: white, spotted regularly with black-brown on wings and tail, face dirty and dusky. Second-winter: intermediate, spots smaller, face less dusky, some already adult-like; full adult dress at two years. Bill thick, blue-grey with a yellow tip, occasionally reddish; iris dark with a narrow dark red orbital ring; legs short and black.
arcter: Breeding adult: crown and nape solid black, cheeks and upper throat white; upperparts and upperwing even pale grey, underparts grey-toned, primaries translucent from below with a narrow black line along the outer trailing edge; tail white. Winter: forehead and crown white. Juvenile: no grey belly, cap not reaching the forehead, back brownish and streaked, dark carpal bar, short streamers. Bill uniform dark blood-red without a black tip when breeding, black in winter; legs and webs short, red, grey-black in winter.
blackc1: Male: olive-grey to dark grey above, nape paler grey, neat black cap; light grey below, silvery white on chin, throat and upper breast; flanks faintly brownish; tail dark grey, olive-edged. Female: cap reddish-brown, upperparts browner. Juvenile: as female, rufous tinge above, olive breast and flanks; first-winter males brown, black or mixed cap. Bill and long legs grey; iris reddish-brown in the English source, always dark in the German.
y00478: Very pale in every plumage; no black anywhere in wing or tail. Adult pale grey above with white trailing edge, white head, neck, breast, underparts, rump and tail; winter head streaked brownish onto the breast. Juvenile and first-winter grey-buff, upperwing paler than the body; second-winter near-white with grey vermiculation on head, nape and breast-sides. Adult bill yellow to yellow-green with red gonys spot, red orbital ring, pale yellow iris; legs pink to greyish flesh. Juvenile bill dark, eye black.
lotjae: Adult: glossy black cap and face, grey to grey-brown back and coverts, contrasting near-black primaries with no white flash; neck-sides, nape and throat white to faintly yellowish, breast white shading gradually into brown-grey belly and vent; underwing lacks a pale primary-base flash. Juveniles in light, intermediate and dark morphs, colder and greyer than Parasitic. Bill dark in summer; juveniles show a pale blue-grey bill base contrasting with a dark tip.
comchi1: Brown-washed dull green above, rump often brighter green; off-white below, yellowish on the flanks, throat and breast variably yellow and buff, flanks washed beige-brown in autumn. Short yellowish-white supercilium, clear before the eye and vague behind; dark eyestripe splits the pale eyering; lower face and ear-coverts dark. Worn birds duller and browner. Bill fine, dark horn with an inconspicuous pale orange base and sides; legs dark brown to grey-black, rarely paler brown.
norwhe: White rump and tail with a bold black inverted-T terminal band in all plumages, central feathers wholly black. Spring male: grey crown and mantle, white forehead and supercilium, black lores and ear-coverts forming a mask, black wings, buff throat and breast, whitish vent. Autumn male browner, wings pale-fringed. Female duller, wings brown, lores not black. Bill black.
reebun: Male breeding: black head and throat, broad white neck collar and white moustachial stripe, dark-streaked brown back, greyish rump, pale underparts washed and streaked brown, heaviest on the flanks; white tail-sides. Grey feather fringes veil this after the autumn moult, wearing off through winter. Female: streaked brown head, buff supercilium, black-and-white malar, chestnut lesser coverts. Bill dark and usually small; legs dark.
eurmag1: Head, neck, breast and vent glossy black with green and violet sheen; belly, flanks and scapulars pure white; primaries mostly white on the inner webs, a conspicuous flash in the open wing; tail black glossed green and reddish purple; rump black with a variable white band. Juvenile sootier and matt, tail shorter, outer scapulars greyish. Bill and legs black and fairly stout; iris dark brown. Juvenile has a pink malar region and somewhat clear eyes.
litgre1: Summer adult unmistakable: blackish-brown above, crown and hindneck black with a faint green sheen, lores and chin black, throat, cheeks, neck-sides and lower neck rich rufous; flanks blackish-brown with pale flecks, underparts glossy white. Winter and juvenile: rufous replaced by dull brownish-grey, buff-toned with darker back and cap; juvenile face streaked black and white. Bright yellow gape patch at the base of the bill; juvenile bill yellow with a small black tip, darkening to black with age.
pomjae: Three morphs. Light adult: black cap running below the bill, yellow neck-sides, white neck crossed by a dark breast band, blackish-brown above, white breast and underparts. Dark morph all dark brown, intermediates paler below and on the head. All morphs show a white primary flash, a diagnostic double flash beneath. Central tail feathers elongated 5.5–11 cm, spoon-shaped, twisted. Bill brownish with the strong downward hook of all skuas; feet black.
atlpuf: Forehead, crown, nape, back, wings and tail glossy black, a broad black collar round neck and throat, underparts white, a diffuse dark grey zone along the flanks. Large lozenge-shaped very pale grey face patch tapering to a point at the nape, with a crease from the eye to its rear tip. Winter face dark grey. Bill blue-grey, yellow and red with a round yellow gape rosette; iris brown to very dark blue, red orbital ring; legs and feet bright orange.
blkgui: Summer: entirely brown-black, green-glossed when fresh, with a big oval white patch on the upperwing formed by the outer greater and median coverts; underwing-coverts and axillaries largely white. Winter: head and underparts white, upperparts barred grey and white, rump white, wing pattern retained. Sexes alike. Juvenile darker and browner; immatures' wing patch mottled grey-brown, visible far off. Bill black; mouth lining bright coral-red and prominent in display; legs and feet coral-red in summer, pale red in winter.
eursta: Iridescent black glossed purple and green, spangled with white and buff feather tips — heavily speckled in winter, plain glossy black by spring as the tips wear away. Flight and tail feathers blackish-brown with pale fringes, secondaries broadly gloss-edged. Female less glossy, keeps her spotting better in breeding dress. Juvenile grey-brown, throat paler, faint pale supercilium, no gloss. Bill blackish in winter, yellow in summer — male's base blue-grey, female's whitish-pink; legs pinkish- to greyish-red; iris dark brown, paler in the female.
rebmer: Male: black head and upper neck glossed green, ragged two-part crest, broad white collar, pale rusty breast spotted black, black back with a white stripe, white vent and speculum crossed by black bars. Female: red-brown head and upper neck merging into greyish lower neck and breast-sides, white below, crested. Juvenile: as female, shorter crest, smaller white wing patches. Bill long, narrow, straight, red with a black upper ridge; feet red.
santer1: Upperwing pale grey, underparts and neck white; primaries darken through the summer. Breeding: crown wholly black with a shaggy black nape crest. Winter: forehead and crown extensively white, crest worn. Sexes alike. Juvenile: back and wings scaly, tail dark-tipped, bill all-blackish, sometimes yellowish at the base only. Bill long, thin and black with a pale yellow tip; legs short and black.
goldcr1: Olive-green to yellow-green above, buff-white to grey-white below; two whitish wingbars from pale covert tips; face plain and pale with no white stripe over the eye, the dark iris standing out. Crown stripe edged by broad black: male yellow with an orange centre, usually covered by the yellow fringing feathers, female wholly yellow. Juvenile duller, no coloured crown. Bill small, thin and black, the nostrils covered by two bristle feathers; legs dark flesh-brown; iris dark.
shttre1: Upperparts dull grey-brown, bark-coloured, intricately patterned black, buff and white, rump rufous; supercilium weak and off-white; underparts dingy white, contrasting with a clean white throat and browner on the rear flanks and vent. Sexes alike. Juvenile whitish below, sometimes with a buff belly.
graher1: Ashy-grey above with white banding on the back and elongated pale grey scapulars; greyish-white below with some black on the flanks; white head and neck with a broad black supercilium ending in a slender dangling crest, and three rows of black streaks down the foreneck; primaries grey-black. Immature duller, head stripe grey, face paler, crest small. Bill long, straight, powerful, pinkish- to yellowish, brighter in breeding adults; iris yellow; legs very long, brown in one source, yellow in another.
eurgre1: Male grey-green above, yellow-green below, rump paler green; cheeks, neck, nape and greater coverts grey, flanks pale grey, throat dirty yellow; outer webs of the primaries yellow, making a yellow-green wing panel and a yellow edge to the closed wing, and the tail-bases yellow too. Female duller, browner above, faintly streaked throughout. Juvenile whitish below with grey streaks. Bill pale horn; legs flesh-coloured, dark sandy in female and juvenile; iris dark in all.
lottit1: Mainly black and white with variable grey and pink: black mantle, wine-red to rufous scapulars, black white-edged tail. Head and underparts vary geographically — northern caudatus pure white-headed, sharply black-naped, no breast band, white belly, white or pink flanks; europaeus and rosaceus have a broad dark band through the eye and reddish-tinged underparts; alpinus darker-faced, black-bibbed, shorter-tailed. Bill black, short and fine; eye peppercorn-black with a yellow-orange upper lid.
mewgul: Adult bluish-grey above, white head, neck, underparts, rump and tail, broad white trailing edge; wingtip black over the outer six primaries with large white mirrors on p9–p10 and white tips. Winter head grey-streaked. Juvenile scaly grey-brown above with a broad grey-brown breast band and broad dark tail band; first-winter has a grey saddle. Bill and legs yellow, varying orange- to greenish-yellow, duller in winter when a blackish band crosses the bill tip; iris brown, red orbital ring.
arcloo: Breeding: grey crown and hindneck; black, purple-glossed throat and foreneck; white necklace of short lines on lower throat, long white stripes down neck-sides onto chest; blackish above with bold white squares on mantle and scapulars, white spots on lesser and median coverts; flanks and underparts white. Non-breeding: upperparts plain blackish-grey, chin to foreneck sharply white. Juvenile: browner. Bill black to blackish-grey, pale grey in non-breeding; legs black outside, grey inside; webs grey or flesh; iris deep brown-red.
comter: Breeding adult: black cap, pale grey upperparts, very pale grey underparts, white rump and tail; outer primaries darker than inner, so the wing looks two-toned, a grey wedge appearing as the shafts wear. Non-breeding: white forehead and underparts, dark carpal bar. Juvenile: brown crown, ginger forehead, brown-scaled back, dark grey secondaries tipped white. Bill red with black tip or all black; legs orange-red. Non-breeding: bill black or red-based, legs dark red to black.
comhom1: Steel-blue head, mantle, upperwing and tail; broad white rump; underparts wholly white, underwings included; short legs and feet feathered white. Sexes alike. Juvenile: sooty to brownish black above and dull, some coverts and quills tipped and edged white, chin dirty white. Bill small and black; eyes brown; toes and the bare parts of the legs pink.
glagul: Very pale in every plumage, no black in wing or tail. Adult: pale grey above, otherwise white, head and neck grey-mottled in winter; primaries translucent from below. Juvenile in a dark and a pale morph: finely vermiculated grey-buff, or nearly all white. Second winter coarsely grey-blotched; grey mantle from the third winter; adult at four years. Bill thick, yellow with red gonys spot; iris pale yellow, orbital ring yellow or orange; legs pale pink. Juvenile: pink black-tipped bill, dark iris.
grecor: Largely black; upperwing-coverts bronze with glossy black fringes, giving a scaled look, body glossed purple, wings and tail bronze to green. Breeding: broad white throat patch, white-flecked crown and nape with a loose crest, white thigh patch. Non-breeding: no thigh patch, duller, nape dark. Juvenile: brown-black with white breast. Bill stout and grey, dark at the hooked tip, paler at the base; gular skin yellow, edged white; iris deep sea-green, duller grey in juveniles.
comcra: Slate-grey overall, darkest on back and rump, palest on breast and wings. Forehead and lores blackish, crown a bare red patch, cheeks and neck black, a white streak from behind the eye to the upper back. Primaries, secondary tips, alula and tail-tip black. Juvenile: yellowish-brown feather tips, plain sandy head, feathered crown, no plume. Iris either red or yellow, the two types unrelated to sex or age; very dark in juveniles.
pifgoo: Body mid grey-brown, head and neck a richer dark brown; back and forewing pale bluish-grey, flight feathers blackish-grey; rump and vent white; tail grey with a narrow pale band inside a broad white tip. Bill short, black at base and tip with a bright pink band across the middle; feet pink.
comgol: Male: green-glossed blackish head with a large round white patch between bill and eye, black above, white neck and belly. Female: brown head, grey body, white belly, variable white neck-ring. Eclipse male female-like but head darker brown, often keeping breeding pattern on the wing. Juvenile: as female, no collar, browner, white wing panel smaller. Iris golden-yellow; female's pearl-white, juvenile's pale grey. Female's grey bill has a yellow and black tip; legs orange-yellow to reddish.
stodov1: Blue-toned grey with no white on rump or wing; two short blackish bars on tertials and greater coverts; broad dark grey band at the tail-tip; wing broadly black-edged, showing a dark trailing edge in flight, underwing dark grey. Breast washed pinkish-purple; neck-sides iridescent green to purple. Sexes alike; juvenile lacks the neck patch. Bill pink with a yellow tip; eyes dark.
eurser1: Dark-streaked greyish-green above, breast and flanks heavily streaked, rump bright yellow and contrasting; narrow yellow wing-bar. Male: lemon-yellow face, neck-sides and breast, forehead, throat and central breast unstreaked; long pale supercilium framing a dark cheek with a pale centre. Female: paler, rump greener yellow. Juvenile: no yellow, brown-green. Feet reddish to dark brown; iris brown.
elefal1: Two morphs. Light: dark grey to grey-brown above with ochre feather edges, whitish lower cheek, throat and neck, bold black moustachial stripe; rufous-brown underparts boldly black-marked, trousers finely streaked; long rufous tail finely barred, subterminal band broadest. Dark: uniformly sooty grey-brown, underparts a shade paler, underwing-coverts black against paler flight-feather bases. Juvenile: pale below, wingtips and coverts darker.
stonec4: Summer male: black head and upperparts, orange-red throat and breast, belly and vent white; white half-collar on the neck-sides, small white scapular patch, very small white rump patch, usually brown and dark-streaked. Female: brown above and on the head, duller, no white neck patches or white rump; only the scapular patch white, and often buffy.
thbmur: Black to blackish-brown on head, neck, back and wings, white below; small rounded black tail; secondary tips white, primaries dark brown. The black throat runs onto the fore-breast so that a white inverted V shows on each breast-side. Winter: lower face white, less so than Common Murre; flanks unstreaked. Bill slaty black with a white stripe along the upper mandible; gape and tongue yellow; feet pale red to grey- or green-yellow.
blkter: Breeding adult: head, neck, breast and belly deep black, back and upperwing even dark grey with a white forewing, underwing pale grey, vent and undertail-coverts white, tail brownish-grey. Non-breeding and juvenile: black cap running down the nape and behind the eye, rest of head, breast and belly white, dark patch on the breast-side at the wing base, upperparts pale grey. Bill black; legs dark, red-black; in winter and juvenile plumage orange-red.
redpha1: Breeding female: dark brown and black above, red below, white cheek patch, blackish-brown crown. Male a duller version, crown light brown. Non-breeding: pale grey above, white below, face and most of the crown white, black patch behind the eye always present. Juvenile: grey-brown above, buff below, dark eye-patch. Bill yellow with black tip when breeding, more yellow on the female; black in winter.
norlap: Black and white, mantle glossed green-grey with a blue-violet shoulder patch; white face crossed by a diffuse black band under the eye; black crown drawn into the crest; black throat and sharply cut black breast-band; belly white, vent rusty-orange; broad white band on the inner wing. Female: shorter crest, less contrast. Winter: chin and foreneck white, face buff, upperparts buff-scaled. Bill black; legs dark red to brown.
crelar1: Dark grey-streaked brown above, whitish below and greyer than Skylark; outer tail feathers light brown with rusty edges; underwing reddish in flight; no white edges to wing or tail. Sexes alike; young more spotted on the back. Crest conspicuous at all times, raised further in display and song.
eurkes: Male: blue-grey head, rump and tail, the tail plain with a broad black end band; back light chestnut with small black diamond spots; underparts pale cream, lightly marked, underwing-coverts near white. Female: head uniformly rufous, back barred dark, tail brown with several bars and a broad end band, underside darker and more spotted. Both show a prominent black malar stripe. Cere, feet and a narrow eye-ring bright yellow, paler in juveniles; bill yellow at the base, dark towards the tip; iris and claws dark.
eurcoo: Slate-grey to blackish above with a brownish to olive sheen, head and neck velvety black, throat and lower neck darker; whitish trailing edge to the wing. Sexes alike. Juvenile: grey-brown, paler on face-sides and breast, no shield, iris dark. First winter: shield smaller, a dark spot inside the white bill-tip. Bill white to faintly pink, about 30 mm, running into a bright white frontal shield 14–30 mm long; iris red to dark red-brown; legs green.
blared1: Male slate-grey above, forehead black, sometimes with a white forehead spot; lores, cheeks and chin to belly black; whitish panel on the secondaries (western birds); belly and undertail blackish-grey, or orange-red in eastern birds. Rump and tail rusty-orange in all plumages, central pair dark brown. Female grey to grey-brown. First-summer male duller, lacking the wing panel. Bill brown-black; legs black and slender.
eugplo: Upperparts grey-brown spangled gold, buff-yellow and white. Breeding male: black throat and belly framed by a white S-shaped band running from forehead to flanks — the most distinctive feature. Female also dark below but far less contrasting; the black is highly variable, so sexing is not always possible. Northern birds blacker and more contrasting, southern paler. Underwing and axillaries white.
egygoo: Boldly marked, unmistakable: pale head with a brown eye-mask, red-brown upperparts, beige-grey underparts and a dark red-brown belly patch. Large white wing panels are hidden by the coverts at rest and blaze out when the bird is alarmed or in flight. Tone varies individually, greyer to warmer brown. Juvenile lacks eye and breast patches until four to five months old. Bill varies from pale red to deep red, reddest on escaped birds; dark patch round the eye.
spofly1: Dull grey-brown above, off-white below, essentially unpatterned; crown, throat and breast finely streaked dark, the streaking heavier on breast-sides and flanks. Wing and tail feathers thinly pale-fringed; in fresh plumage buff tips to median and greater coverts make a paler line on the wing. Sexes alike. Juvenile: ochre-buff spots above, scaly brown spots below. Bill blackish horn with a paler base to the lower mandible; legs black; iris dark brown.
hoopoe: Body beige-orange to buff. Wings boldly barred black and white with distinct yellow tones; tail black with a broad white band across the last third and white at the base. Crest tipped black and white, usually laid back like a nape-tuft, raised straight up when excited. Female slightly smaller and a shade duller. Bill black with a fawn base.
brambl: White rump in every plumage, and an orange breast contrasting with a white belly. Male in summer: glossy blue-black head, nape and mantle; throat, breast and lesser coverts unspotted rusty-orange; flanks dark-spotted. Female duller — grey-brown head with two faint dark crown-stripes, warm brown mantle, orange-buff breast. Winter male brown-grey-headed; wear reveals the breeding dress gradually. Bill straw-yellow with a black tip in winter in both sexes, black in the summer male.
rocpig: Head, neck and breast dark blue-grey with glossy yellowish, greenish and red-violet iridescence along the neck. Best mark is the white lower back; the two black bars across the pale grey wings are also distinctive. Tail with a black terminal band, outer webs edged white; underwing pale. Female's neck gloss weaker; juvenile duller. Feral birds endlessly variable. Bill grey-black with a conspicuous off-white cere; iris orange, red or golden-yellow with a paler inner ring; bare eye-surround bluish-grey; feet pink-red.
comrav: Adult uniformly black, glossed metallic green or blue-violet according to the light; throat feathers elongated and lanceolate, standing out clearly when calling; bases of the neck feathers pale brownish-grey. Juvenile: gloss almost absent, brown-black above and brown below, throat feathers not elongated, tail less wedge-shaped. Bill and legs black, feet stout and strong; iris dark brown, blue-grey in the juvenile, gape pinkish at first.
eucdov: Uniform pale grey-buff to pinkish-grey, slightly darker above than below; back and lesser coverts browner, greater coverts pale blue-grey, flight feathers dark grey. Black white-edged half-collar on the nape is the key mark, missing on autumn juveniles. Long tail broadly white-edged, dark grey and white-tipped below; blue-grey underwing patch. Legs short and red; bill black to dark grey; iris red with a narrow white eye-ring, looking black at any distance.
rocpip1: Smoky-olive above, weakly streaked darker; underparts buff, heavily but poorly defined streaked brown — the whole bird looks dark and blurred. Pale eye-ring; tail-sides grey-white. Sexes alike, males average brighter but overlap completely. Immature browner and more streaked above. Eastern littoralis in summer can show pinkish underparts and a pale supercilium. Legs, bill and iris dark brown or blackish.
gragoo: Grey-brown and paler than the other grey geese; head darker, breast and belly pale with variable black spotting; neck faintly lined by the rows of feathers. Pale grey forewing and rump obvious in flight or on a stretched wing; white line along the upper flanks, vent white. No white on the head. Juvenile browner, belly unspotted. Bill large, wholly pale, orange-pink to red-orange with a white or brown nail; legs and feet dull pink.
yelgul1: Adult: head pure white even in autumn; back grey, a shade darker than Herring Gull, paler than Lesser Black-backed; more extensive black in the wing-tip, with few white mirrors. First-year paler on head, rump and underparts than Herring Gull, recalling young Great Black-backed; dark bill and eyes, dark flight feathers, sharp black tail-band. Adult-like by second winter. Legs bright yellow; bill yellow with a large red gonys spot spreading onto the upper mandible; iris lemon-yellow, orbital ring red.
eurjay1: Body light rufous-brown to pinkish-buff. Forehead and crown whitish streaked black, raisable into a crest; white throat set off by a bold black moustachial stripe about the length of the bill. Rump, belly-centre and undertail-coverts white, the rump conspicuous against the black tail. Wing barred black and white with a bright azure panel finely barred black. Bill grey-black to black; feet grey-brown to brownish flesh with yellowish soles; iris bluish-grey with reddish rings and fine speckling.
snobun: Contrasty black, white, brown and grey. Breeding male unmistakable: white head, neck, rump and underparts with black back and wing-tips; most secondaries, primary bases, coverts and outer tail feathers white. Female in breeding dress has grey-brown crown, nape and ear-coverts, brown wash on back and breast. In winter both show broad orange-brown fringes on the back. Bill black in summer males, otherwise yellow with a black tip; legs black.
comeid: Male: white back and breast, breast faintly pink-flushed; black crown, belly, flanks, rump-centre, tail and tail-coverts; pale moss-green nape, feathers slightly lengthened into a small crest. Female: brown, told from all ducks but other eiders by size and head shape. Subspecies differ slightly in drake bill colour, from yellow-green to bright orange-yellow. Drake's bill yellow-green in breeding plumage, otherwise blue-grey to green-grey; bill sides feathered to the nostrils, leaving two bare wedges towards the eye.
yebwar3: Greenish to greyish-green above with blackish wings, whitish below. Two prominent yellowish-white wingbars from the tips of the greater and median coverts, the greater-covert bar the longer; tertials broadly yellow-margined; long broad yellow supercilium with a dark eye-stripe beneath it. Some show a faint pale central crown-stripe, many do not. Legs brownish-pink.
retloo: Breeding adult unmistakable: dark grey head and neck-sides with narrow black-and-white stripes down the hindneck, a triangular rust-red throat patch, white underparts and a plain dark grey-brown mantle — the only loon with an all-dark back. Non-breeding: chin, foreneck and much of the face white, crown and hindneck grey, mantle speckled white. Juvenile as winter but duller, neck greyer. Bill dark grey, pale grey in winter; iris carmine-red to burgundy; legs black outside, pale inside, webs pinkish-brown with darker margins.
wiltit1: Long dull sooty-black cap running back onto the mantle, and a black bib often broadening downwards; cheeks white, reaching right up to the nape; back grey-brown, underparts buff with distinctly rufous flanks. Pale buff edges to the secondaries make a light patch on the closed wing. Sexes alike, juvenile like the adult. Eastern birds much paler than western. Bill short, stubby and black; legs grey; iris black.
redpol1: Brownish-grey to whitish above with dark streaks; bright red patch on forehead and crown, black bib, black feathering round the bill-base and a very fine black loral line. Two pale wingbars. Adult male's breast rose-red in spring, white or barely tinged in winter; female's yellow-grey. Rump streaked; broad dark brown streak across the vent. Bill yellowish with a dark tip; legs brown; iris dark brown.
lcspet: All black except a paler grey-brown bar across the secondary coverts, a slightly paler greyish face, and usually a white rump with a hint of a dark divide down the middle. The pale greater coverts read as a light half-circle above when the bird banks and shows its back. Dark-rumped birds occur off western North America.
marwar3: Upperparts grey-brown, greyer on the back than reed warbler; underparts yellowish-white; throat whitish. Sexes alike.
renpha: Breeding male: grey-brown above, black face, white throat, orange-brown neck patch smaller and duller than the female's. Female: slate-grey above, orange-red patch on the foreneck reaching the cheeks. White wing stripe. Juvenile: grey and brown above with yellow bands, black crown, black patch behind the eye. Winter grey above, white below; black eyepatch always present.
commer: Male: black green-glossed head and back, crest smooth and rounded, body white with a salmon-pink tinge, grey rump and tail, wing white on the inner half, black on the outer. Female: red-brown head with white chin, cut sharply off the pale neck, ash-grey above, white below. Juvenile: as female, plus a short black-edged white stripe from eye to bill. Bill and legs red to brownish-red, brightest on adult males, dullest on juveniles.
grcgre1: Summer adult unmistakable: black forehead, crown and nape with erectile black tufts, white cheeks, black lores, pale yellow between forehead and bill; elongated chestnut ear- and cheek-feathers form a black-edged ruff. Foreneck, breast and belly white; hindneck, back and rump blackish-brown; flanks pale grey-buff. Winter: whiter, plumes gone, white above the eye. Chicks boldly black-and-white striped. Bill red with a brown ridge and pale tip, paler in winter; iris dark red with a pale orange ring; legs and lobes greenish grey.
comswi: Sooty to brownish-black throughout except a small greyish-white chin patch, hard to make out at any distance or in flight. Sexes alike. Juvenile: darker and less glossy, the white of the throat more extensive and purer, with white feather fringes. Bill small, black, slightly downcurved; iris deep brown; feet short, blackish flesh-coloured, all four toes forward with sharp curved claws.
eupfly1: Male: pitch-black above, in some areas dark brown, white below, with a large white wing patch, white tail sides and a small white forehead patch. Female: pale brown above, no forehead patch, white below. Non-breeding males and juveniles have the black replaced by pale brown, and are then very hard to tell from other Ficedula. Bill black.
eurlin1: Male: grey head and nape, crimson forehead and breast, chestnut back and coverts, whitish brown-streaked throat, yellowish-brown streaked underparts, grey-white streaked rump. White outer webs of the primaries make a pale patch at rest and in flight; tail brown-black, white-edged. Red duller in autumn, veiled by grey fringes. Female and juvenile: no red at all, streaked brown above and below. Bill short, conical, grey.
gnwtea: Male: chestnut head with a broad iridescent green crescent running from before the eye to the nape, thinly edged creamy-white; buff breast spotted brown; finely vermiculated grey body, white belly, white scapular side-stripe; butter-yellow triangle each side of the black stern. Female: dark brown above with rufous feather edges, buff-brown below with dark spots. Speculum green above, black below. Bill sides orange to greenish in both sexes.
eursha1: Glossy greenish-black throughout, with no white anywhere; yellow throat patch. Breeding adult carries a crest of elongated crown feathers curling forward. Juvenile: more red-brown than a young cormorant, with darker underparts and paler feet. Bill dark with a yellow base, pale yellow in juveniles; bare skin round the bill yellow, black with yellow spots on the throat; feet black.
cetwar1: Upperparts rich chestnut to dark reddish-brown; throat and breast pale grey-brown, dirty grey-white below with brownish tones on flanks and belly. Narrow, washed-out pale grey stripe arching over the eye. Sexes alike, but males 26–32% heavier with wings 11–13% longer. Juvenile: as adult, plumage fresh, two dark spots on the tongue. Iris black and conspicuous.
yellow2: Male: brilliant yellow head and throat, narrow dark eye-stripe behind the eye, longish dark moustachial; back heavily streaked brown, rump unstreaked rufous, belly yellow, breast and flanks rusty with fine streaks, outer tail feathers white. Female: duller and browner, more streaked on crown, breast and flanks, throat still yellowish. Juvenile: much duller, rump paler. Winter birds less strongly marked.
rebshr1: Male: chestnut back and scapulars, pale blue-grey crown and nape, narrow black mask through the eye, swallowing the eye at distance, sometimes edged by a faint whitish supercilium; grey rump; underparts tinged pink; black-and-white tail like a wheatear's. Female: brown and vermiculated above, greyer nape and rump, darker mask, underparts buff and vermiculated. Juvenile: as female, vermiculated above as well. Iris dark; bill strong and slightly hooked.
bkhgul: Summer adult: chocolate-brown hood, black at distance, narrow white eye-crescents, open in front; white neck, underparts and tail, pale grey mantle and coverts, black primary tips. Winter: hood gone, dark smudge above and spot behind the eye. Juvenile: mottled brown with ochre in the grey mantle, black tail band, white rump; first-winter grey-backed, keeping carpal bar and tail band. Bill and legs red in summer, iris dark brown; winter bill paler red, tip blackish; juvenile legs yellow-orange, bill yellow with a black tip.
redkno: Breeding: back and coverts mottled grey, orange, white and black; face, throat, breast and underparts cinnamon-red, rear belly paler. Female slightly lighter, eye-line less distinct. Winter: uniformly pale grey above, pale below, white supercilium, grey-spotted breast and flanks. Juvenile: like winter adult but buffier on the breast, back and coverts scaled dark inside pale feather tips. Bill short, straight, dark, with a pale almost white ring round the base; legs short, dark grey-green, olive-yellow in juveniles.
relpar1: Sandy-brown above; crown warm pinkish-brown, forecrown and crown edges pale blue-grey, narrow off-white supercilium. Black lores broaden behind the eye and run round the creamy-white throat into a black gorget that breaks into broad black streaks over the pale blue-grey breast. Belly pinkish-buff; flanks with eight to ten bold rufous bars edged black. Outer tail feathers rufous, hind neck browner. Bill red; bright red eye-ring above a patch of pinkish-red bare skin on the lores; legs pink to red.
blksco1: Male all black, with a yellow patch in the middle of the bill and a small knob at the bill base. Female brown-grey with pale cheeks and a blackish-brown crown. No white anywhere on the drake and none in the wing; the female's pale areas are more extensive than in other scoters. Legs blackish-brown to blackish-grey in both sexes; male's bill shows yellow around the nostrils.
eurnut2: Blue-grey above, black eye-stripe, whitish throat and cheeks; flanks and lower belly orange-red, undertail-coverts mottled white, upper tail-coverts red-brown with large white spots. Tail black but for the grey central feathers. Caesia, the widespread western form, is orange-buff below with white throat and cheeks; arctica large and pale, white-fronted, eye-stripe reduced, more white in wings and tail. Bill stout, dark grey, paler at the base of the lower mandible; iris dark brown; legs and feet pale brown or greyish.
comshe: Boldly pied: dark green head and neck, white body with a broad chestnut breast-band, black belly stripe, black scapular bands and black primaries. Wing-coverts white, secondaries black with strong green gloss in flight, outer tertial orange-brown, inner tertials white. Female slightly smaller, usually with white flecks on the green face. Juvenile greyish above, mostly white below, adult wing pattern already. Bill reddish-pink, bright red on the breeding male and then with a prominent knob at the base; feet pink.
eurwoo: Cryptic: upperparts intricately patterned reddish-brown, black and grey; underparts buff-white with a rusty wash and brown wavy barring. Head and nape barred crosswise with black, not striped as in the snipe. Primaries black-brown with red-brown and rusty cross-spots; tail black with red-brown bars and grey tips. Sexes alike in colour. Bill pale flesh with a dark rounded tip; legs grey to pinkish, feathered to the foot; eyes large and black, set high and far back.
tufduc: Male: black head, breast, upperparts and tail, flanks and belly white; tuft long and hanging. Female: brown, darker on back and head, flanks paler, some with white round the bill base but never as extensive as in the scaups; tuft shorter. Eclipse male dark brown with slightly paler flanks. Juvenile: duller grey-brown. White wing-band in flight in both sexes. Bill blue-grey, broadening to a black tip; iris golden yellow, striking in both sexes.
eaywag1: Male: olive to grey-green above, yellow below; back, flight-feather edges, underparts and undertail-coverts yellow, tail feathers black; throat and breast bright yellow; head pattern of breeding males varies by subspecies. Female: duller, back greyer, throat and breast pale yellow. Juvenile: less contrasted, browner above, paler and less yellow below.
bargoo: White face and forehead, so a black line runs from bill-base to eye; crown, nape, neck and breast black against a white belly. Upperparts silver-grey barred black and white; back dark grey, rump black, undertail white; tail white with a broad black terminal band; adults show pale grey vertical flank bars. Juvenile: browner, flank bars ill-defined. Bill small, stubby, black; legs black to dark grey. Sexes alike.
grywag: Male: upperparts cool grey, rump and uppertail-coverts greenish-yellow; narrow white supercilium, dark lores, broken white eye-ring; breeding throat black, edged by whitish moustachial stripes; underparts yellow, deepest on the undertail-coverts, whiter mid-flank. Tail black, yellow beneath, outer feathers white; white wing-band shows in flight. Other plumages lack the black throat. Bill black; legs and feet flesh to brownish horn; iris dark brown, eye ringed white.
eurgri1: Sexes alike. Body, leg feathering and lesser and median coverts pale brown to light rufous with pale buff streaking, contrasting with near-uniform blackish-grey flight and tail feathers; greater coverts and tertials blackish-brown broadly edged pale brown, forming a pale band on the upperwing. Head and neck densely white-downed; ruff loose, white. Juvenile: ruff narrow, lanceolate, pale brown. Bill stout, yellowish horn to green-yellow, pale grey at the base; cere, bare parts of legs and toes grey.
eurspa1: Male: upperparts slate-grey, sometimes bluish; underparts finely barred rufous, looking plain orange at distance. Female: dark brown to greyish-brown above, barred brown below. Juvenile: warm brown above with rusty fringes, coarsely barred or spotted below, throat streaked but with no central stripe. Tail with four or five dark bars in both sexes. Iris orange in the male, yellow in the female, pale yellow in juveniles; cere and legs yellow, claws black; bill black, blue-grey at base.
misthr1: Pale grey-brown above; chin and throat greyish-white; yellowish-buff breast and off-white belly marked with round black spots, denser on the lower breast; throat centre unspotted, often a dark patch each side of the upper breast. Outer tail feathers white-tipped, underwing-coverts white. Sexes alike. Juvenile: paler above with creamy teardrop centres, smaller spots below. Eyes dark brown; bill blackish with a yellowish base to the lower mandible; legs and feet yellowish-brown.
azwmag3: Glossy black cap reaching below the eye; white throat, standing out sharply in shade against a grey-brown bird. Back pinkish-brown, breast and belly buff; wings and long tail pale azure-blue, obvious in sunlight. Iris dark brown to black; bill, legs and feet black. Sexes alike.
sibjay1: Greyish-brown; head and crown dark brown with paler forehead, chin and throat grey, breast buff; rump, tail sides and undertail rusty-red, central tail feathers ash-grey; wing bend rufous, showing best in flight; rufous streaking on the outer feathers. Sexes alike, female slightly smaller. Juvenile: browner mantle, plainer overall. Bill and legs black; eye black; nostril feathering forms a small buff tuft at the forehead.
skylar: Upperparts beige to reddish-brown, crown, back and rump finely streaked blackish-brown. Upper breast and flanks clearly dark-streaked on yellowish-white, ending abruptly against the unstreaked white belly. Broad yellowish-white supercilium ending behind the rufous, pale-rimmed ear-coverts; broad white malar, white throat. Wings dark grey-brown with a whitish trailing edge; outer tail feathers white. Bill horn-coloured, lower mandible paler at the base; legs light brown.
eursis: Male: black cap and chin-bib, rest of head yellow with green cheeks; back greyish-green, rump yellow; wings black with a bold yellow wing stripe; tail sides yellow, tip black; breast yellowish, whiter and streaked towards the vent. Female: olive and streaked, cap and ear-coverts greenish, bib white, rump whitish-yellow. Juvenile as female, duller. Legs and feet dark brown; eyes black.
rerswa8: Adult: crown and upperparts blue-glossed black, wings dark above; rump, nape collar and sides of head rusty-red; face, throat, diffusely streaked breast and belly buffy, cut off sharply by black undertail-coverts and tail, so the tail looks dipped in ink; no breast band, no white tail spots. Juvenile: duller greyish above, rump whitish-buff, streamers shorter.
ictwar1: Uniform brownish olive-green to grey-green above, evenly light yellow below, the yellow deepest on throat and fore-breast; breast sides and flanks washed brownish. Pale lores, short pale yellow supercilium, pale eye-ring. Secondaries and tertials broadly pale-edged, forming a pale panel on the closed wing. Sexes alike. Autumn juvenile slightly paler. Iris dark brown; bill two-toned, upper mandible dark brown, lower yellow to orange; legs lead-grey, sometimes bluish.
dunlin: Breeding: crown and back dark with rufous fringes, throat and breast whitish finely dark-streaked, flanks spotted, belly solid black — unique among waders of this size. Non-breeding: plain grey-brown above, pale grey breast band against white below. Juvenile: buff-brown above with two weak whitish V's on the back, black marks on flanks or belly. Bill black; legs black to blackish-olive; iris brown-black.
gyhchi: Cap dark grey-brown, not black, darkest next to eye and bill; throat black; cheeks and area below the eye white; mantle warm cinnamon-brown, back paler grey; flanks rusty-brown, belly whitish-grey. Wing and tail dark above but with clear pale fringes giving a paler grey cast; underwing pale. Whole pattern looks washed-out. Bill black; eye black.
smew: Male unmistakable, 'cracked ice' or 'panda' white with fine black lines and a black patch between bill and eye; back partly black; looks very black-and-white in flight, with oval white wing-patches. Female and immature grey with chestnut forehead and crown, white chin and cheeks, black lores — 'redhead' smew. Eclipse male female-like but keeps more white in the wing. Bill short and grey; males are bigger-billed than females.
blagro1: Cock: blue-black, darkest on neck and breast, head, neck and rear back glossed steel-blue shot with violet; white wingbars and wing patch, undertail-coverts white, tail white beneath; bare intense red crescent over each eye, swelling in the breeding season. Hen: cryptic brown, darker above, whiter on the belly, tail relatively short. Juvenile: barred black and rusty-buff above. Iris brown; bill short and stout, horn-black; feet brownish.
bulpet: Very dark sooty-brown throughout, looking almost wholly dark; paler greater coverts form a pale diagonal band along each upperwing; underwing uniformly dark. Bill black; feet flesh-coloured.
eurcur: Mainly greyish brown; head, neck, breast and upperparts pale beige-brown streaked and spotted dark; cheeks finely streaked and contrasting with the pale chin and throat; breast more strongly streaked, paling towards the belly. White rump and back form a white wedge in flight. Sexes alike. Legs greyish blue.
grewhi1: Male: grey head, white throat, pink-tinged breast, broad white eye-ring. Female: head tinged brown, breast pale buff, throat duller; first-winter birds like the female. Both grey-brown above and whitish below with light brown flanks; wing and covert feathers black with broad rufous fringes; tail grey-brown with white outer edges. Legs yellow-brown to buff; iris red-ochre in the male, brown in the female.
whimbr5: Mainly greyish brown; crown strikingly dark brown, split by a pale cream central stripe; broad dark eye-stripe, narrow dark loral streak; back, breast and flanks densely spotted. Back and rump white in phaeopus and alboaxillaris; tail grey-brown, barred; dark 'hand' to the wing. Bill long and curved, longest in adult females.
greegr: Wholly white. No plumes on the hindcrown; instead long, loose scapular and back plumes (aigrettes) grown for breeding, spread wheel-like in display. Sexes identical; juvenile like a non-breeding adult. Bill yellow to orange-yellow, often dark-tipped, blackening with a yellow base when breeding; lores and orbital ring greenish-yellow, emerald when breeding; legs black; iris yellow.
whisto1: Mainly white with black flight feathers and wing coverts; breast feathers long and shaggy, forming a ruff raised in courtship. Sexes identical. Younger birds show a dark bill-tip. Bill and legs bright red, the colour diet-derived; iris dull brown or grey; peri-orbital skin black.
rolhaw: Upperparts nearly uniform cinnamon-brown; round head and nape pale brown to grey; narrow dark line from eye to yellow bill-base; underparts mottled, with a broad brown chest-band and belly almost always black against a paler breast; square black carpal patch against white underwing in pale morphs; tail white with a sharp black terminal band. Juvenile: very pale below, tail-band diffuse. Bill small, yellow at the base; legs feathered to the toes, the feathering pale grey to white with dark shaft-streaks.
gadwal: Male finely grey-vermiculated; crown dark brown, rest of head pale brown; breast, scapulars and flanks dark grey; rear end black above and below; brilliant white speculum, black behind it, chestnut on the coverts; belly whitish. Female: brown, mallard-like, chin and throat white. Eclipse male female-like but keeps the wing pattern. Juvenile: head greyer than the warm brown body. Male's bill blackish-grey; female's short and orange-yellow with an unbroken dark ridge; legs orange-yellow to bright yellow; eyes dark.
woosan: Summer adult: back coarsely vermiculated grey, white and beige, brown with darker mottling; small diffuse brownish spots on neck and breast, merging gradually into the white belly. Winter: greyer, breast plainer. Juvenile: browner, finely spotted beige above. Bold white supercilium in all plumages, running well behind the eye to the nape. Small, weakly contrasting white rump-patch; underwing pale grey-brown. Bill short, fine, grey-black; legs long, pale yellow-green.
taibeg1: Grey-brown; head and neck darker brown than the body; upperparts dark brown with narrow white feather fringes; breast pale grey, belly whitish towards the tail; fine white lines on flanks, wing edges and tail-tip; upper wing-coverts dark brown, not pale grey. Bill black at base and tip with an orange mid-band, its width varying by race; nail dark; legs and feet orange; iris dark brown.
eugwoo2: Dark green above, pale yellowish to grey-green below, rump bright green-yellow; crown and nape red; black mask from bill to behind the eye; ear-coverts, chin and throat whitish; wings brown-black spotted yellow-white; tail green-grey, blackish-barred. Male: moustache red-centred, black-bordered. Female: moustache solid black. Juvenile: much duller, heavily dark-spotted and barred below, red of head dull and grey-flecked, upperparts white-spotted. Iris bluish-white; bill and feet lead-grey.
comloo: Breeding adult: head and neck glossy black, ending abruptly against the white breast; black neck-ring and white necklace of parallel streaks; mantle chequered with large white squares, rear back and flanks finely white-spotted; underparts white. Non-breeding: dark grey-brown above, throat and foreneck white, blackish half-collar, white round the eye. Full breeding dress only from the fourth calendar year. Bill large and straight, dark grey to black, sometimes pale-tipped; greyish-white with dark culmen in winter; legs and feet grey; iris red.
bohwax: Mainly rust-grey-brown; black mask through eye to nape, finely white-edged in adults; white streak behind bill, white curve below eye; black throat; lower belly chestnut; rump grey; tail black-banded with bright yellow tip; primaries black, yellow-edged with white 'fishhooks'; secondaries tipped with red sealing-wax droplets. Male: yellow tail-tip 6–11 mm, throat sharply defined, 6–8 waxy tips. Juvenile: throat whitish, grey-streaked. Iris dark brown; bill mainly black; legs dark grey or black.
gwfgoo: Greyish brown, paler below; light grey breast dappled with dark brown to black blotches and bars; white undertail-coverts and a broad white band on the outer tail; upper wing-coverts mouse-grey, flight feathers dark. Adult has a white blaze from bill-base to forehead, not reaching the crown. Juvenile: no blaze, no belly bars, black bill-nail. Bill pink in European birds, yellow-orange in Greenland flavirostris; legs bright orange.
eutspa: Crown and nape wholly rich chestnut; cheeks pure white with a kidney-shaped black ear-patch; chin, throat and bill-base black; pale collar almost closed on the nape. Upperparts light brown streaked black, heaviest on mantle and scapulars; rump yellow-brown; breast and belly brown-grey; two narrow white wing-bars. Sexes identical. Juvenile: duller, crown greyer-brown, cheek and throat patches sooty grey. Bill lead-blue in summer, almost black in winter; legs pale brown.
lotduc: Complex moult, at least three plumages a year, all pied white, brown and black, with wholly dark wings and white underparts. Male winter: white head and neck, dark cheek patch, dark breast, mostly white body; summer: head, neck and back dark, cheek patch white. Female: brown back, short pointed tail; head white with dark crown in winter, dark in summer. Male's bill dark grey crossed by a pink band, often all black outside the breeding season.
compoc: Male: head and neck chestnut, breast and stern black, body pale grey finely vermiculated, back pale blue-grey; eclipse as breeding but the black washed out to grey. Female: head grey-brown all year with pale patches at bill-base and behind the eye, darker below the eye; breast dark grey to light brown; body pale grey but looking dirty; stern dark grey. Male's bill dark with a broad blue-grey band, iris orange-red; female's band smaller or absent, iris brown, pale eye-ring; juvenile iris yellow-olive; legs grey throughout.
wooshr1: Male: upperparts largely black, underparts nearly white; crown and nape rust to orange-brown; scapulars and rump white, sometimes closing in a V on the back; white primary bases show as a wing-window at rest, a broad white band in flight; tail black. Female: duller, black greyer, crown more orange, slightly smaller. Juvenile: vermiculated brown, grey and white above, buff below.
wilpta2: Male in spring: head, neck and upper breast deep red-brown, cut off sharply from white below; tail black; a large red comb over each eye. Late summer: breast and upperparts grey-buff, comb a red line. Female: combs tiny, brown more barred, white belly flecked brown. Winter: both sexes white but for black outer tail. White eye-ring always; wings white year-round. Bill short, broad, thick and dark; combs above the eyes red; tarsi and toes feathered.
thelar1: Crown and upperparts grey-brown, boldly blackish-streaked, finer on the nape; whitish supercilium, dark eye-stripe, pale orbital ring, whitish dark-edged malar; underparts whitish, breast-sides and flanks washed buff-brown; lower throat and breast spotted, condensing into strong streaks; underwing-coverts and axillaries grey; rump plain grey-brown, uppertail-coverts rusty.
