Sexes alike. Juvenile: crest shorter, back spotted, breast less streaked. Bill short, dark horn, with a paler base to the lower mandible.
lirplo: Back and wings grey-brown, breast and belly white with a single black neckband; cap brown, forehead white, black mask through the eye with white above. Sexes alike. Race dubius: orbital ring distinctly broader, with a large red patch at the bill-base. Bill short and dark, red at the base; legs flesh to brown-yellow; iris black with a conspicuous yellow orbital ring.
comgre: Pale in all plumages: grey above with black spotting, white below, breast finely vermiculated black on white; brown-toned when breeding, grey-brown in winter. In flight a long, broad white wedge runs up the back onto the tail, sharply against grey-black upperwings; no white in the wing. Legs long, grey-green to yellow-green with age and season; bill long, stout, grey at the base.
corplo: Grey-brown back and wings; white belly and white breast cut by one broad black neckband; brown cap, white forehead, black mask through the eye; white wingbar. Female: head markings and breast band often carry much brown. Juvenile: duller, breast band often incomplete and grey-brown. Bill short, dark at the tip, orange to yellow at the base; legs orange to yellowish; iris black.
wescap1: Cock dark grey to dark brown, breast a metallic green shield; belly and undertail-coverts black to white by race; tail black, often white-spotted at mid-length; lesser coverts white, a spot at the wing bow. Female: brown above barred black and silver, paler and buffish-yellow below, throat and breast plain orange-brown, tail rufous with coarse black bars. Bare swollen red skin over the eye in both sexes; bill yellowish-white in older birds, darker in young ones.
zitcis1: Sandy-brown above, heavily streaked black; whitish to leather-yellow below, the buff deeper on the female; rump rufous. Tail dark beneath with a broad white rear edge above and pale tips. Male has less crown streaking and bolder back marks than the female; supercilium only hinted; no nuchal collar. Breeding male's bill dark, the female's pale; legs dark beige to orange.
tawowl1: Two morphs, rufous-brown or greyish-brown above, with intermediates; dark brown lengthwise blotches above, finely vermiculated between; underparts whitish streaked brown, vent white with brown arrow marks; large white spots on scapulars and greater coverts; tail barred brown and rufous, whitish-tipped. Facial disc plain, dark-rimmed, two whitish strokes above it. Female more rufous. Bill thick, strongly hooked, sulphur-yellow with a horn to pale grey base; iris blackish-brown, pupil blue-black; eyelids bare, pale red.
ibgshr1: Head, nape, mantle, back and rump lead-grey, crown and nape darkest; broad black mask from the bill base over the eye to behind the ear-coverts, edged above by a fine white supercilium; cheeks and throat white; breast and belly pink-flushed, strongest on the flanks; scapulars white against black flight feathers; moderate white patch on the primaries. Juvenile: less distinctive.
ruff: Back grey-brown and scaled, underparts white. Breeding male unmistakable: head tufts and a neck ruff, black, chestnut or white, solid, barred or irregular, with extensive black on the breast. Female and non-breeding birds plain and scaled, without ornaments. Juvenile: broad cinnamon to cream feather edges, coarsely scaled above, crown streaked black. Legs dark greenish in juveniles, pink to orange in adults, red on breeding males; bill dark, orange-red or pink; eye small and dark.
norpin: Male: chocolate-brown head, darker crown, near-black stripe down the nape, white breast with a narrow white wedge up the neck-side; grey upperparts and sides, long grey black-striped scapulars draped over the back; yellow vent against the black undertail, central tail feathers to 10 cm. Female: mottled and scalloped light brown, head plainer grey-brown, tail shorter but pointed. Bill bluish grey, long and slim; legs blue-grey.
pursan: Summer: dark above with a faint purple gloss, scapulars grey-black turning rufous inwards with white fringes; mostly white below with grey-buff vermiculation, breast smeared grey, rump black. Winter: darker and plainer, head, breast and upperparts uniform grey-brown, no supercilium. Juvenile: paler breast, strongly orange legs, yellow bill base. Legs short and yellow, mustard-yellow in winter, bright orange on juveniles; bill dark with a yellow base.
comnig1: Warm light brown above, tail and rump distinctly rufous; buff to dirty white below, breast lightly mottled brown. Sexes alike. Eastern and Caucasian races paler above with a stronger face pattern, including a pale supercilium. Bill pink and yellow; eye black, ringed white.
perfal: Adult bluish-black to slate-grey above with indistinct darker barring and black wingtips; white to rusty below, cleanly barred dark brown, foreneck and upper breast lightly spotted. Crown black; heavy black moustachial stripe set sharply against pale neck sides and a white throat. Tail barred, black-tipped with a white terminal band. Juvenile: much browner, underparts streaked rather than barred. Cere, eye-ring and feet yellow; bill grey with a darker tip to nearly black, notched near the tip; claws black; iris dark brown.
leswhi4: Brown to grey-brown above, crown and short tail greyer, whitish below with faintly buff flanks; throat white. Surest mark the sharply defined grey ear-coverts, a darker bandit mask through the eye. Sexes and ages alike. Race blythi has a paler grey crown cut off from the cheek by a white supercilium; minula paler and browner, althaea larger and darker. Bill short and dark with a paler grey-blue base; legs and tarsi dark; iris dark, lower eyelid pale, a thin light grey eye-ring.
trepip: Yellow to olive-brown above with diffuse blackish streaks, sharper on the crown; rump and upper tail-coverts greener and barely streaked; cream to yellowish below, throat, breast and neck sides yellower, breast boldly streaked and flanks much less so; outer tail feathers partly white; two pale wingbars from light-edged coverts. Bill with a pink base.
coatit2: Head, throat and neck glossy blue-black, with a large brilliant white nape spot drawn out as a stripe; face sides off-white, tinged grey or yellow by race; upperparts bluish- to olive-grey; two white wingbars from white-tipped coverts; underparts whitish, buff to rufous on the flanks. Juvenile: duller, head not glossy, nape and cheeks tinged yellow. Bill black; legs lead-coloured; irides dark brown.
wfspet: Pale brown to grey above — crown grey-brown, nape and back dark grey — with black flight feathers; whole underside, underwing-coverts and face white, cut by a dark grey-brown mask over eye and cheek; grey neck sides run onto the breast sides; black tail set off against an ash-grey rump. Juvenile: broader pale fringes above, shallower tail fork. Bill, tarsi, toes and claws black; webs yellow.
firecr1: Bright olive-green above with a bronze patch on each shoulder; whitish below washed brownish-grey on breast and flanks; two white wingbars. Head boldly marked: black eye stripe, long white supercilium, black-edged crown stripe mainly orange in the male, bright yellow in the female; neck sides vivid yellow-green. Juvenile: greyer and duller, no crown colour, head markings weaker. Bill tiny, pointed and black; legs brownish-black.
banswa: Dull grey-brown to earth-brown above, wings and tail blackish-brown; white below with a broad, clear brown band across the breast; throat white. Juvenile: rufous tips to the coverts and pale margins above, chin grey-buff instead of white. Bill black and flat; legs and toes brown.
eugori2: Male brilliant yellow with black-violet wings and tail; yellow wing patch, yellow tips and edges to the tail, central tail feathers black-violet narrowly edged yellow and the outer ones yellow; black lore from bill base to eye. Female: olive-green above, yellower towards the rump, dirty white below with fine dark streaks, tail dark green to black, lore fainter and greyer. Bill pink to rust-red; iris brownish, tending to reddish; legs dark blackish-violet.
sedwar1: Back and wings streaked brown; crown streaked black with dark side bands and a dark brown central band; prominent whitish to buff-yellow supercilium; rump warm brown and unstreaked, contrasting with the duller wings; throat whitish, underparts pale and yellowish. Sexes identical. Juvenile: dark spots on the breast and an apparent pale central crown stripe against darker edges. Legs greyish.
rudtur: Harlequin pattern of brown, black and white in all seasons. Breeding: reddish-brown above with black marks, head mainly white with black crown streaks and a black face pattern, breast black with a white patch at the sides, rest white. Female duller, head browner and more streaked. Non-breeding: grey-brown above, black-mottled, head dark. Juvenile: pale brown head, pale fringes, scaly. Legs short, about 3.5 cm, and bright orange, duller yellow-brown on juveniles; bill dark.
garwar1: Lack of marks is the mark: unstreaked olive-brown to grey above, dull whitish below; buff wash on throat and flanks; dirty-white rump; uniform wing-coverts; whitish eyering, faint pale supercilium; grey wash on neck sides. Sexes alike. Juvenile: looser plumage, paler and greyer above, buff below, pale fringes to flight and tertial feathers. Bill blue-grey to beige, grey upper mandible, paler lower, darker tip; legs bluish- to light grey; eye black.
comred1: Breeding: marbled brown, mottled black and grey above, variably brown-and-white below; head finely streaked, short cream supercilium, white eyering. Winter: plainer grey-brown above, white below, breast washed grey and finely streaked. Juvenile: warmer brown above with cream feather fringes, breast buff-brown, underparts dark-streaked. Bill orange-red at base, black-tipped; legs dark red when breeding, orange-red in winter; juvenile legs orange-yellow, bill mostly grey.
redkit1: Body, upper tail and wing-coverts rufous; head and neck whitish, brown-streaked; underparts red-brown with black shaft-streaks. White primary patches contrast with deeply fingered black wing-tips and dark secondaries; tail rufous, barred blackish. Female as male. Juvenile: washed-out, breast buff with pale streaks, tail less deeply forked with a dark subterminal band, pale tips to all greater coverts.
gyfwoo1: Head and nape plain light grey; male with a small red patch on the forecrown, female without but with fine black crown streaks. Narrow black line across the lores and a small black moustache like a downturned mouth-corner. Back, scapulars and coverts olive-green; rump yellow-green; underparts pale grey to grey-green; folded primaries barred brown-black on grey-white. Bill dark and very slightly upcurved; iris dark, sometimes glinting reddish depending on the light.
comred2: Male summer: slate-grey crown, nape and back; white forehead and supercilium; face and throat black; breast and flanks orange-chestnut fading whitish on the belly; rump and tail bright orange-red, central feathers dark brown. Autumn male washed out under pale feather fringes. Female: grey-brown above, buff-white to light orange below, throat usually whitish; tail as male. Bill and legs black.
batgod: Breeding male: neck, breast and belly unbroken brick-red, dark brown above; female duller, chestnut to cinnamon below. Non-breeding: plain grey-brown with darker feather centres giving a striped look, whitish beneath, head, neck and breast grey-streaked. Juvenile as non-breeding but buffier, flanks and breast streaked. Tail barred; no white wing-bar. Legs blue-grey to dark grey; bill bi-coloured, pink at the base, black towards the tip.
eurtre1: Upperparts warm brown, intricately patterned black, buff and white, the mantle spotting white and contrasty; rump rufous; tail plain brown. Underparts clean white; belly, flanks and vent tinged buff; supercilium white. Sexes alike. Juvenile: duller above, underparts dull white with fine dark spotting on the flanks.
norsho: Male: dark iridescent green head, black at range or in poor light, white breast and back, chestnut belly and flanks, black stern; bright pale blue forewing separated from the green speculum by a white border; white face crescent in early autumn. Female: mottled beige and brown, pale face with darker crown and eye-stripe, forewing grey. Juvenile: much darker, chestnut-toned. Male's bill black or very dark grey, iris yellow, legs bright orange-red; female's bill grey with orange cutting edges, eye dark.
woolar1: Dull pale brown above, crown and upper mantle finely streaked dark and pale buff, rump plain brown; underparts white, upper breast finely dark-streaked. Bold white supercilia meeting in a V on the nape; ear-coverts rufous; broad white malar, dark grey chin-stripe, white throat. Black-and-white greater primary coverts mark the bend of the folded wing; tail tipped white. Bill slender, brown-grey, paler at the base; legs yellowish brown to flesh-coloured.
hawfin: Light brown, head orange- to red-brown joined to the dark brown back by a broad grey nape band; underparts reddish-brown to brownish-white. Black mask round the eye, and a black throat patch. Wings blue-black with a white greater-covert band, crescent-shaped in flight; tail black, broadly white-tipped. Female paler, grey panel along the secondaries. Juvenile: grey-yellow breast, coarsely spotted belly. Bill blue-black in summer, bone-white to pale yellow-brown in winter; legs and toes short and pinkish flesh; eyes brown.
melwar1: Plain brown-green above — browner than icterine — and light yellow below. Lores, eyering and sides of the bill pale. Wing uniform: no pale panel formed by tertial and secondary edges. Sexes alike, the male often stronger-coloured; juvenile much paler overall with a faintly indicated pale wing panel. Legs brown to brownish; bill strong and pointed.
eurwar1: Brown above, the back often with a faint olive-grey tone, rump warmer rust-brown; underparts buff to yellowish white, throat whitish. Unstreaked throughout. Sexes identical; young birds richer buff below. Legs grey-brown.
bbspet1: Head, neck, upperparts, throat, upper breast and tail black-brown; white rump band; belly white with a broad black stripe down its centre linking the dark head to the black undertail-coverts — extent of white varies individually, and the stripe may be broken or absent. Flanks white; underwing white with dark leading edge and dark flight feathers. Juvenile as adult. Bill, legs and feet black.
eurhob: Slate-grey above with a dark crown; white cheeks and unstreaked white throat set against a strong dark face mask with a clear but short moustache — two short black stripes. Underparts whitish, boldly black-streaked; thighs and undertail-coverts unstreaked rufous, the red trousers. Sexes alike. Juvenile: much browner, scaled above, thighs and undertail-coverts buff and streaked. Cere and feet yellow.
litgul: Adult summer: black hood; pale grey back and upperwing, white rump and tail, underparts white with a rosy flush; underwing dark grey with a narrow white trailing edge running to the tip. Winter: white head with black cap and ear-spot. Juvenile: blackish back and head, bold dark W across the upperwing, white underwing; second year near-adult with some black primaries. Bill dark red-brown in summer, looking black at range, black in winter; legs bright red, duller pink-red in winter; iris dark.
blrwar1: Plain olive- to greyish-brown above, lacking the warmer tones of its relatives, the short rounded wings less olive; underparts plain off-white, flanks more olive-grey than buff. Short whitish supercilium from the bill-base to just behind the eye, with a dusky stripe through the eye; tertials uniform, without contrast. Sexes alike; juvenile yellower below. Bill greyish brown, lower mandible pale pinkish-brown at the base with a diffuse dark tip; legs pale pinkish-brown.
eubeat1: Crown, nape, mantle and inner secondaries chestnut, wings green; throat bright yellow, cut from the turquoise belly and vent by a black line; rump and outer primaries blue-green; scapulars yellow-white; black face mask, white forehead. Female tends greener rather than gold on the shoulders. Non-breeding much duller, back blue-green, tail streamers absent; juvenile like non-breeding but plainer. Bill black, long and slightly decurved; iris red.
sheowl: Mottled tawny to brown on a straw ground, coarsely flecked red-brown with white teardrops on back and scapulars; wings and tail barred. Upper breast heavily streaked, contrasting with a very pale, almost unstreaked belly. Underwing white with a black comma at the outer coverts and black tips; broad white trailing edge above. Ear-tufts minimal, seldom visible. Bill short, strong and black; iris yellow to yellow-orange in a black ring, set in a large whitish facial disc.
blueth: Best mark in all plumages: two-toned outer tail — basal half rust-red, terminal half black-brown; plus a clear whitish supercilium. Male breeding: chin, throat and upper breast silky bright blue with a rust-red centre (svecica), white (cyanecula) or plain (magna). Upperparts dark grey-brown. Female: cream throat with a blackish crescent, little or no blue. Juvenile freckled dark brown, then female-like. Bill thin, dark horn-brown to blackish, bright lemon-yellow inside; legs dark horn-brown, tarsus reddish translucent; iris blackish.
whwsco3: Male glossy black with a small white mark below and behind the eye and a large white wing patch; bill dark with an orange-yellow side field, base slightly swollen, no knob. Female brown, duller and unglossed, pale spot between eye and bill, often a pale cheek patch. Both sexes show white secondaries as a wing patch, often visible swimming. Feet red; male's iris blue-grey, female's darker.
harduc: Male: slate-blue head and neck with a large white crescent before the eye running to the crest, a round white dot behind it and an oval white streak down the neck-side; black crown stripe with chestnut sides; white black-bordered collar and breast bar; chestnut flanks; white inner secondaries over the folded wing. Female: brown-grey with three white head patches. Bill blue-grey; eye reddish.
steeid: Male (November–June) near unmistakable: white head with black chin, black eye and eye-ring, pale green nape patch and a fainter one before the eye; black collar, back and stern; cinnamon-pink underparts with a black spot on the breast-side at the waterline; long white-striped purple-black tertials, white shoulders. Female dark to cinnamon brown, pale eye-ring, blue-purple speculum white-bordered both sides. Bill grey, long and squarish with a straight upper edge; legs and feet dark bluish grey.
booeag1: Two morphs. Pale: underbody and underwing-coverts white against black flight feathers, three inner primaries paler and barred, fine brown streaks on the crop. Dark: uniformly dark brown, inner primaries still paler. Both: mottled upperparts, broad pale beige-brown band diagonally across the median coverts, pale nape and uppertail-coverts, white 'landing lights' on the forward scapulars, white at the bill base. Bill dark with a yellow cere; legs yellow; iris golden-yellow in adults, brown in juveniles.
kineid: Male: black body, white to salmon breast, powder-blue crown and nape, sea-green cheeks, white chin and throat; white wing-covert patches, white patches at the black rump sides, two triangular tertial 'sails' over the black scapulars. Female: warm rust-brown with blackish chevrons, fine dark head streaks, buff spot at the bill base and a buff eye-ring drawn back downcurved. Bill coral-red with a large orange-yellow frontal knob set off by a thin black line; female's bill black or grey and shorter; legs greenish grey.
merlin: Male: slate blue-grey above with a rusty nape, buff to orange underparts heavily streaked dark, grey tail with a black terminal band. Female and juvenile: grey-brown to dark brown above, whitish buff below spotted and streaked brown, tail strongly barred. Face weakly patterned — faint whitish supercilium, indistinct malar; remiges blackish, tail with three or four wide dark bands. Cere yellow; blue-grey in juveniles.
tunbeg1: Head and neck grey-brown, the head distinctly darker than the neck; upperparts dark brown with narrow grey-white feather fringes; breast pale grey, belly whitish. Upperwing-coverts dark brown with narrow white fringes. Bill short and stout, mostly black with an orange band across the middle and a dark nail, lamellae showing; legs and feet orange to yellow-red.
bktgod: Breeding male: head, neck and breast orange to deep rust, belly white barred black to a variable extent, crown streaked; female duller. Winter: plain brown-grey breast and upperparts, mantle and wings pale grey. Juvenile: pale orange wash on neck and breast. White tail base with a broad black terminal band all year. Bill orange-pink at the base with a dark tip in summer, pink with a black tip in winter; legs dark grey, brown or black.
grnsan: Upperparts dark greenish-brown spotted white, boldest on breeding adults and faint in winter and on young birds; head and breast grey-brown, finely streaked, cut off sharply from the white underparts. Broad white tail base, tail tip barred black. Legs and short bill dark green.
comsan: Upperparts greyish olive-brown, in breeding plumage finely dark-marked and irregularly barred, mantle bronze-glossed; breast-sides brown-grey spotted and cross-barred, with a white wedge pushing up between them and the wing; underparts white. Winter plainer and duller with more barring on the wings. Juvenile more heavily barred above with buff feather edges. Sexes alike. Bill medium-long, dark brown with a pale orange-brown base; legs short, pale yellow; eye black.
norhar1: Male: pale blue-grey above and across the upper breast, white below, black wingtips, dark trailing edge to the wing, white rump. Female: brown above with white unstreaked uppertail-coverts — a 'ringtail' — underparts buff barred brown. Juvenile: as female but barring less distinct, secondaries dark brown, belly less barred. Iris pale in young birds, dark in adults.
grewar3: Upperparts grey-green to olive-green, underparts grey-white to off-white; long pale to yellow supercilium reaching almost to the hindcrown, often broadened and upturned at the rear; dark eye-stripe, not reaching the bill base; one narrow white wing-bar, often barely visible. Sexes alike. Legs brown; lower mandible paler than the upper, with no dark tip.
blawoo1: Entirely black; upperparts darker and glossier, sometimes shimmering bluish, underparts duller and a shade paler, tinged dark grey or blackish-brown; primaries often paler and browner; worn birds matt charcoal. Male: whole crown red. Female: red confined to the hindcrown. Juvenile: less glossy, crown duller red, throat paler grey. Bill grey-white to bone-white with a distinct dark grey tip; iris pale cream, looking white at distance; toes pale grey, claws darker.
comros: Male: head, upper breast and rump carmine-red with a broad dark lore; belly and undertail-coverts white to pale grey; back, wings and tail dark brown with two narrow, indistinct wing-bars. Female and males up to the third calendar year: dull olive-brown and streaked, buff below, wing-bars rusty-buff — inseparable from each other. Juvenile: more intensely olive-brown, bars clearer. Bill stout and dark; eyes dark.
gargan: Male: red-brown head and breast finely vermiculated white, a broad white crescent sweeping from over the eye to the nape, dark crown; loose grey scapulars, white tertial edges, pale grey-blue flanks and belly; pale blue forewing, white border. Female: vermiculated beige-grey-brown, dark cap, dark eye-line, pale lore spot; grey speculum edged white front and rear. Bill grey, fairly long, paler grey on the female; legs grey.
litegr: Entirely white, though dark forms are largely bluish-grey. Breeding: two long narrow nape plumes forming a crest, looser-barbed breast plumes and elongated scapulars up to 200 mm; in winter the scapulars are short and normal. Juvenile: as non-breeding adult, sometimes with a few greyish or brownish feathers. Sexes alike. Bill and lores black, iris yellow, bare facial skin greenish-grey turning red in high courtship; legs black, feet yellow — juveniles greenish-black legs, duller feet.
wemhar1: Male: cryptic reddish-brown, pale yellowish streaks heaviest on the breast, head and shoulders pale greyish-yellow, mid-wing panel silver-grey, tail grey, primaries black — three-toned brown-grey-black in flight. Female: chocolate-brown with pale yellow crown, throat and forewing edge and a dark stripe through the eye, the pale eye standing out; no grey in wing or tail. Juvenile: as female, less yellow. Bill black with a yellow cere; legs, feet and irides yellow.
osprey: Upperparts uniform deep glossy brown; underparts and underwing-coverts brilliant white, the breast with a brown band that is broader and darker on the female. Head white with a broad, sharply demarcated dark brown stripe through the eye to the nape. Blackish greater under-coverts form a dark carpal patch. Juvenile: pale-scaled above, crown white streaked dark, tail finely barred. Bill black, cere lead-grey blue; iris golden to brown, orange in juveniles; feet white with black talons, toes equal, the outer one reversible.
loeowl: Ochraceous-tawny with a grey or brown wash, overlaid with blackish vertical streaks heaviest on wings and back; scapulars marked whitish; dark carpal patches and broad buff to almost orange panels at the base of the primaries; flight feathers clearly barred. Underside paler, upper breast dusky-streaked, below that a herring-bone pattern. Female darker and rustier. Iris bright orange-yellow; tarsus and toes fully feathered.
rengre: Breeding: black cap running below the eye, pale grey cheeks and throat, rusty red neck, dark grey back and flanks, white underparts. Winter: duskier than other grebes — grey cap ill-defined, merging into a grey face, a pale crescent curving behind the ear-coverts; foreneck whitish, hindneck darker. Juvenile: striped face, diffuse blackish cap, pale red neck. Bill long, pointed, black with a yellow base — yellow duller in winter, extensive on juveniles; eye dark brown.
whinch1: Male: blackish face mask ringed by a white supercilium and malar, orange-buff throat and breast, brown upperparts mottled dark, whitish belly, small white patches on the greater and inner median coverts; rump the same colour as the back; tail dark with white bases to the outer feathers. Female: duller, mask browner, supercilium and malar buff, wing patches small or absent. Legs grey-black; bill short, straight, grey-black; iris black.
spored: Breeding: sooty-black, small white spots above. Winter: grey above, whiter below, white supercilium sharply marked; wings plain, no wing-bars; white rump running up the back as a white wedge. Juvenile: grey-brown finely speckled white above, underparts pale and closely barred. Bill red on the lower mandible only; legs long, dark red.
rocpet1: Strong whitish supercilium over a dark brown eye-stripe; paler grey-brown median crown stripe; cheeks, ear-coverts and neck-sides pale grey-brown; mantle grey-brown streaked dark; rump and uppertail-coverts grey-brown; breast and flanks diffusely streaked grey-brown; lemon-yellow spot on the lower throat, diagnostic but hard to see. Sexes alike; female's throat spot smaller and paler. Upper mandible brown, lower yellowish with a dark brown tip; eyes pale grey-brown; legs pale flesh to horn.
cretit2: Crest patterned black and white. Upperparts grey-brown; sides of head and neck white, enclosed by a black crescent starting behind the eye and by a white collar cut off below by a black band that forms a triangular bib; throat black; underparts dirty white, flanks cream. Sexes alike.
spaspa1: Male: chestnut crown, whitish cheeks, narrow white supercilium; black bib breaking up into heavy black streaking over breast and flanks; back streaked. Female: grey-brown throughout and boldly marked, pale cream supercilium, broad cream streaks on the back, light streaking on the sides, faintly grey-streaked below.
brnowl: Facial disc very pale — white to pale grey or faintly rufous — with black eyes, like a flat mask with oversized oblique eye-slits. Head and upperparts pale brown to grey, often golden-brown finely speckled grey. Underparts vary from pure white to pale brown; subspecies differ markedly, guttata darker-backed with a yellow-orange breast. Bill pale yellow; iris dark brown to black; claws horn-coloured; toes nearly bare, dark grey-brown.
shteag1: Underside predominantly white, often almost unmarked; chin, throat and upper breast pale earthy brown; underwing lightly barred; tail with three or four bars. Upperparts grey-brown, the pale white-flecked upperwing-coverts contrasting with dark brown secondaries and near-black primaries. Iris bright yellow.
horgre: Breeding: black head with erectile golden-red ear tufts and black fan-shaped cheek feathers; neck, flanks, lores and upper breast chestnut; crown and back black; belly dull white. Winter: white neck, chest and cheeks against a dull black-grey crown and back, the border running in a straight line behind the eye. Juvenile: duller, back brown-tinged, crown line less distinct, bill paler. Bill blue-grey to black, base flesh, tip near-white; iris intense red when breeding, pink at rest, narrow silver-white ring; legs grey, feet blue-green.
whtdip1: Head and nape plain mid-brown; upperparts slate-grey scaled darker by brown fringes, looking black at distance; wings and tail browner. Throat and upper breast brilliant white, bordered below by a warm chestnut band merging into black on belly and flanks; nominate birds blackish-bellied. Juvenile: scaled grey above, white only on the chin, breast and belly mottled pale grey. Bill almost black; legs and iris brown; claws strikingly pale, almost white.
gresca: Male: head black glossed green, breast and tail black; back pale silver-grey vermiculated, darkening rearwards; flanks and belly bright white; white wing-stripe from the speculum along the flight feathers. Eclipse duller, mottled. Female: dull cinnamon-brown, darker-backed, flanks vermiculated, broad white band round the bill base, often a pale cheek patch. Juvenile like female, less white at the bill base. Bill light blue to lead-grey with a small black nail; iris bright yellow, brown-yellow in juveniles; legs and feet grey.
thrnig1: Upperparts dark brown with a slight olive tinge, never rufous; wings and tail dark rufous-brown; lores and ear-coverts brownish-black; dark eye with a pale rim. Chin and throat pale buff to whitish mottled brown, sides of the throat spotted; breast feathers dark-centred, giving a clouded, mottled breast; undertail-coverts buff, faintly barred brown. Sexes alike; juvenile darker and more mottled. Bill dark brown, paler below; legs and feet pale brown; iris dark brown.
rusbun: Male summer: black head, white supercilium and throat; rufous breast band and nape, rufous-spotted flanks, rufous rump; upperparts brown streaked dark, belly white. Female: crown and cheeks brown-speckled, supercilium dirty white, less rufous on the nape. Autumn: sexes alike, black and rufous hidden under buff-brown fringes. All plumages: white, black-framed spot at the rear of the ear-coverts. Legs pink; lower mandible pink.
temsti: Drab: upperparts and head plain brown, underparts white apart from a darker breast; outer tail feathers white. Breeding adult relieved by some brighter rufous and blackish mantle feathers. Winter: dull grey to greenish- or brownish-grey above and across the upper breast, white below, recalling a tiny Common Sandpiper. Legs dull yellow to brown.
euhbuz1: Adult upperparts almost uniform brown. Male has a blue-grey head, female's brown, and she is slightly larger and darker. Tail with a broad dark terminal band and two narrower dark bars — fewer than in the Buteo buzzards — the barring repeated on the wings. Highly variable: dark, intermediate, pale and rufous morphs, as juvenile and adult. Bill small, slender, blackish-grey; cere dark grey; iris yellow in adults, dark in juveniles; legs yellow, claws black.
norgos1: Male: blue-grey above with darker crown and ear-coverts, underparts white and closely grey-barred; broad white supercilium. Female: brown-grey back and crown, coarsely barred below, fluffy white undertail-coverts. Juvenile: coarsely mottled brown above, buff to white below with drop-shaped dark brown lengthwise streaks; tail with three to five dark bars. Darker ear-coverts are the best adult character. Legs and cere yellow; iris bright yellow in juveniles, turning red-orange in adults.
watrai1: Upperparts forehead to tail olive- to dark brown streaked black, heaviest on the shoulders; head-sides, throat, neck and breast to upper belly dark slate-blue, blackish between bill and eye, breast-sides browner; flanks barred black and white; undertail white with darker streaks. Sexes alike. Juvenile: blackish crown, white chin and throat, barred buff-white below. Chick all black, bill pale. Bill red; iris red; legs flesh-brown.
hazgro1: Upperparts grey washed rufous, blackish barring on head, nape and back; rump greyest; underparts mottled brown, black and white, strengthening towards the throat. Tail grey vermiculated brown, all but the central feathers with a broad black band inside a grey-white tip. Male: black white-bordered throat patch, prominent crest, fine red supercilium. Female: throat pale rufous, crest barely visible.
eurcrm1: Ash-brown to mid-grey above with grey-brown tones, flight feathers evenly dark grey; underparts paler grey with a dark vent. Underwing- and undertail-coverts blackish, contrasting strongly with the rest of the underside. No breast band. Spread tail shows white square spots near the tips of all but the central and outermost feather pairs. Juvenile: buff-brown tips to head, upperparts and wing-coverts. Eyes brown; small bill mainly black; legs brownish-pink.
casgul2: Adult: head, neck, underparts, rump and tail pure white; upperparts pale grey without a bluish tone. Broad white trailing edge running into white primary tips; outermost primary with a large white tip and white tongue up the inner web; black crescent-shaped and covering six primaries. First-winter: pale head, streaked hindneck, greyish back, two pale lines across the coverts. Bill yellow to greenish-yellow, gonys spot orange or red; eye brown to yellow-brown, often looking dark; orbital ring orange or red; legs pink to yellowish.
redcro: Male: mostly red to brick-red, strongest on crown, breast and rump, the rump looking pink when fresh; wings and tail dark brown; some birds yellow, orange or showing green. Female: olive to grey-green or yellow-green, rump yellowish, flanks strongly brown-streaked. Juvenile: grey-brown to greenish-grey, heavily dark-streaked, bill straight at first and crossing only later. Eyes small and dark brown.
martit2: Cap and nape glossy black with a blue sheen, reaching to mid-eye and back into the nape; bib below the bill small and black; cheeks white, evenly narrow, dusky brown on the ear-coverts. Upperparts, wings and tail grey-brown, rump warmer beige, tertials only slightly pale-fringed. Underparts off-white, buff on flanks and undertail-coverts. Juvenile duller-capped and whiter below. Bill black with paler cutting edges; iris dark to blackish-brown; legs dark grey to slate, tinged blue.
itaspa1: Male: crown, nape and sides of head chestnut; cheeks near-pure white; fine white supercilium usually clear; throat and breast bib pure black, more black-flecked than house sparrow; upperparts bright chestnut; lower back and rump brownish, not grey; underparts pale grey, unstreaked. Bib dull when fresh, brightened by wear. Female: as female house sparrow.
rocpta1: Winter: all white but for the black tail; male also black lores and a red comb over the eye. Breeding male: head, neck, upper breast, back, coverts and flanks mottled grey-brown, black, beige and white; wings and underparts white. Female less contrasted. Autumn: grey-speckled, only the primaries white. Bill black and slender; red comb above the eye, largest on the breeding male; tarsi feathered white.
leswoo1: Male: crimson black-bordered crown; face white to cream, framed by black lores, malar and cheek stripe, the last not reaching the black nape band; nape and upper back black; lower back barred black and white, wings broadly barred; outer tail barred; underparts white, flanks streaked. No red on vent or undertail-coverts. Female: crown white. Juvenile: some crimson on the head. Bill slate-grey, long for the bird at up to 18 mm; legs slate-grey.
cinvul1: Uniformly dark brown, looking black at any distance; short bare bluish-pink neck ringed by a dark feather ruff. Female averages slightly heavier and larger than male. Bill tip black; iris brown; legs grey-blue to whitish-yellow, pink in juveniles, whose bill may also be pink.
norshr1: Pearl to ash grey above, always darker than the white underparts; deep black mask from the bill through the eye, broadening on the ear-coverts, edged above by a narrow white supercilium; scapulars white; black wings with one or two white primary-base patches, secondaries white-fringed; long tail black, outer feathers white, near-white below. Female: greyer below, faintly vermiculated. Juvenile: grey-brown, vermiculated. Bill nearly black and hooked, base of the lower mandible paler; legs black-grey.
webwar1: Crown and back dull grey-green with a brown tinge; rump yellow-green and contrasting; wings and tail green-toned with black in them, tertials pale-edged; throat to undertail-coverts white; supercilium whitish but indistinct. Sexes alike. Spring birds often show a pale grey panel formed by bleached, worn edges to greater coverts and tertials. Bill small and pointed; legs brown to pale grey-brown.
pingro: Male: head, breast and rump rose-red to pink, flanks grey. Female: head, breast and rump olive-yellow, back and underparts grey. Both: black wings with double white wing-bars and white tertial edges, blackish forked tail. Older females and young males intermediate, orange or brownish; young birds less contrasting and shaggy while moulting the head.
grebit1: Pale buffy-brown, streaked and barred black throughout; crown and nape black; sides of head and neck tawny-buff barred black; yellowish-buff supercilium, brownish-black moustachial stripe; chin and throat cream-buff with a rusty-brown central stripe; breast and belly yellowish-buff with broad brown side stripes; wings and tail rusty-buff mottled black. Male larger and more strongly marked. Bill green-yellow with a darker tip to the upper mandible, finely serrated near the tip; feet green-yellow.
litowl1: Dark sepia to grey-brown above, spotted, streaked and barred whitish, the spots small and dense on the crown, larger and rounder on the upper back; white V on the nape running into a white nape band; underparts pale, streaked brown; whitish supercilia over a weak facial disc give a frowning, stern look. Juvenile: duller, no white crown spots. Iris lemon- to sulphur-yellow; cere strongly swollen; toes only sparsely feathered.
whbwoo1: Upper back pure black, wholly without white shoulder patches; lower back and rump white, greyer towards the tail; wings strongly barred black and white; yellowish forehead patch; black malar reaching the nape; underparts cream, breast and flanks clearly streaked black; undertail-coverts pink. Male: crown red. Female: crown glossy black. Juvenile: duller, flank streaks broader, crown pale red.
rudshe: Male: orange-brown body, paler orange-brown head and neck cut off by a narrow black collar; rump, flight feathers, tail-coverts and tail black; green speculum on the inner wing; wing-coverts white above and below. Female: whitish head and neck, no collar. Juvenile: as female but darker brown. Colour variable, fading with wear; collar lost after breeding, restored by April. Bill black; legs dark grey.
sarwar1: Male: head black, merging diffusely into the dark grey nape and back; throat white; breast and belly paler grey to whitish; undertail-coverts white; a reddish hue on upper- or underparts varies from absent to pronounced. Female: head grey, back brown, flanks grey-brown, underparts buff to pale brown. Eye red; orbital ring bright red in the male, duller red in the female.
manduc: Male: large white crescent over the eye, reddish face and whiskers, metallic-green crest; purple breast with two vertical white bars; ruddy flanks; two orange sail feathers raised on the back. Female: greyish-brown, slender white eye-ring and stripe back from the eye, paler below, small white flank stripe, weaker crest. Eclipse male: female-like but crestless, breast and flanks clearer yellow-brown. Male's bill small and red, dull carmine in eclipse or bright yellow-orange; female's bill dark with a pale tip.
corcra: Crown and upperparts brown-black streaked buff and grey; wing-coverts distinctly chestnut with a few white bars; face, neck and breast blue-grey, cut by a pale brown streak from the bill to behind the eye; belly whitish; flanks and undertail barred chestnut and white. Female: warmer above, eye-streak narrower and duller. Juvenile: yellower above, buff-brown where the adult is grey. Bill strong and flesh-coloured; iris pale brown; legs and feet pale grey.
bkwsti: Black above, white below and on head, neck and tail; head and neck variably black: usually a grey or black spot behind the eye, sometimes black hindcrown and hindneck. Male: back and scapulars green-glossed. Female: back browner, contrasting with the black remiges. Juvenile: grey rather than black, wings sandy with pale fringes showing as a white line in flight. Legs pink to rose-red, flesh-coloured in juveniles; bill black, straight and needle-fine.
cirbun1: Male: black crown, eyestripe and throat on a bright yellow head; greenish breast band across yellow underparts; flanks chestnut; back chestnut and heavily streaked; rump olive. Non-breeding male duller, brown feathers veiling the face pattern. Female: like female yellowhammer but rump streaked grey-brown to olive, shoulders chestnut, finely streaked above and below. Juvenile: paler, more yellow-brown.
grnwoo3: Green above, rump and uppertail-coverts yellowish; crown and nape red; head almost free of black, the eye ringed dusky grey rather than black. Male: moustache red, bordered black below only, not all round. Female: moustache pale-bordered above, red crown feathers often white-tipped. Bill dark grey; iris white or pink; legs olive-grey.
subwar6: Male: head and back lead-grey, underparts brick to orange-red over the whole belly, not the breast alone; white malar streak. Female: brown-grey above with a greyer head, whitish below with a pink flush. No white wedge on the second-outermost tail feather. Legs pink; eye-ring naked.
rosgul: Summer adult: pale silver-grey above, white below, body flushed pink, a neat black ring behind the head. Winter: collar gone but for a grey stripe each side of the neck; small dark crescent behind the eye; nape and breast grey. Juvenile: white-grey, a dark W across the wings in flight and a big dark carpal triangle, no pink. Bill black in every season; legs red to red-orange, grey-brown to orange in juveniles.
eutdov: Blue-grey head, neck, flanks and rump; cinnamon wings mottled black, each feather black-centred with rufous fringe; vinaceous throat and breast; belly and undertail-coverts white; black-and-white barred patch on neck sides. From below the spread tail shows a blackish chevron on white. Juvenile: browner, duller, neck bars absent. Bill black; legs and eye-rings red. Juvenile legs brown.
eupowl1: Greyish-brown, red-tinged, dotted white above; tail darker with five narrow whitish bars; white to grey "eyebrows", dark facial area; white half-collar on the hindneck; dark occipital marks on the nape that can look like a second face; underparts white to pale, brown-speckled and streaked. Juvenile: as adult but lacking most white spots. Bill greyish-yellow, hooked; legs and toes brownish-yellow, talons black; iris yellow.
darwar1: Male: grey head and back — bluish-grey or brownish-grey in some populations; underparts reddish, throat red spotted white; sides dull grey, clearer on the belly. Female: paler below, especially on the throat, browner grey above, underparts browner, throat spots smaller and fainter. Juvenile: as female. Iris red.
retpip: Breeding adult: brick-red face and throat. Otherwise dull brown above, crown and upper mantle boldly dark-streaked, rump and uppertail-coverts streaked too; whitish mantle stripes; underparts yellowish-white, breast and flanks heavily black-streaked. Female: red confined to throat and upper breast, lost in winter. First-winter: throat white, but strong white supercilium, narrow white eye-ring, pale tertial edges. Bill yellow, as in Meadow Pipit.
syrwoo1: Male: black above with large white shoulder patches and a crimson nape spot; forehead white; face and neck sides white, no black bar from nape to malar, so the cheek looks broad; white-spotted flight feathers form three wingbars; underparts buffish white, flanks faintly streaked; vent and undertail-coverts pinkish-red. Female: no crimson nape. Juvenile: crown crimson, nape spot absent. Bill long, slate black; legs greenish grey; eye black; pale feathering at the nostrils.
blakit1: Uniformly dark brown and weakly contrasted. Adult head, throat and nape pale grey, dark-streaked; darker patch behind the eye; breast and belly paler, often rufous-brown, dark feather shafts giving a streaked look; outer flight feathers black; pale coverts band contrasts with near-black remiges. Juvenile: paler and more mottled with whitish-yellow feather fringes, belly streaked, dark mask through the eye. Cere and gape yellow, upper mandible black, lower yellowish; legs yellow, claws black; iris brown, turning yellow only in old birds.
comqua1: Male: grey-brown, densely marked rufous and black; white shaft streaks form three pale lines along the crown centre and sides; yellowish supercilium; head sides dark-streaked; a rufous band from the gape frames the whitish throat, a brown stripe down the throat centre; chin white; upper breast cream, finely streaked, belly whitish-grey. Female: head pattern weaker, breast and foreneck plain whitish-grey. Bill small and curved in both sexes.
sander: Winter: very pale — light grey above and on the crown, face and underparts white, a dark shoulder patch and dark primaries. Breeding: face, throat and neck brick-red, upperparts brownish mottled, increasingly rufous; belly white. Spring birds greyer, more speckled on head and neck. Juvenile: spangled black and white, far more contrasted than the adult. Bill and legs black.
callar1: Streaked greyish brown to pale sandy above, white below, with a large black patch on each side of the breast and neck; pale supercilium; throat and breast creamy, the breast dark-streaked; tail feathers brown-black with white outer edges. Bill large and thick, brown above, yellowish below; feet brownish-pink; iris brown.
blkswa: Black-feathered throughout with white flight feathers, hidden at rest and flashing only on open wings or in flight; feathers along the wing edges curled. Male slightly larger, its bill longer and straighter. Cygnet: greyish-brown with pale-edged feathers, plain dark silver-grey in down. Bill bright red with a pale bar and white tip; legs and feet greyish-black; iris orange to pale brown.
miswoo1: Crown bright red without a black border; face largely dirty white, black head markings weak and no black loral band; upperparts glossy black with white shoulder patches and broad white barring on the coverts; underparts white, breast pale yellowish, flanks boldly streaked dark grey; belly pink, deepening to red at the vent. Female: crown slightly duller. Bill short, light grey, not powerful.
woowar: Green above, belly white, breast yellowish-white; throat and long, clear supercilium lemon-yellow; pale contrasting fringes to tertials, flight feathers and greater coverts. Sexes alike.
grrwar1: Unstreaked brown above, chin and underparts dull buffish- to yellowish-white, throat whitish; supercilium whitish and not sharply marked, but stronger than Common Reed Warbler's. Sexes identical. Juvenile: richer buff below, back more rufous, supercilium buff-brown.
bahgoo: White head crossed by two black-brown bars, the first arching from eye to eye over the hindcrown, the second shorter and lower on the nape; hindneck black with two white lines down the sides; throat dark grey; body pale silver-grey, belly white, primaries black; tail grey with a white tip, rump and undertail white. Juvenile: lacks the black head bars. Bill light to orange-yellow; feet orange; iris dark brown.
litter1: Summer adult: black crown and black eye-mask separated by a narrow white wedge on the forehead; upperparts grey, underparts white. Winter: forehead and face much whiter, front of the crown and much of the mask lost. Sexes alike. Summer: bill yellow with a black tip, legs orange-yellow. Winter: bill black, legs duller.
nohowl: Dark brown above, spotted off-white on all dorsal parts; head and neck blackish above with white spots; black V on the hindneck; face white with a black border, white eye-surrounds bearing black bristles; underparts white, closely barred dark grey-brown right down to the toes; long tail brown with white bars. Juvenile: greyer-brown, underparts not yet clearly barred. Bill curved, pale yellow; iris yellow.
litbun: Chestnut face and cheeks, with a fine dark border behind them and often a small pale spot at the rear of the cheek; white malar stripe; black crown stripes with a pale central band; bold white eye-ring; lores pale rufous. Upperparts brown, heavily streaked; underparts white, finely dark-streaked on breast and sides. Sexes similar; female duller, winter birds plainer. Legs always pink, never red- or grey-brown.
eurnut3: Mid to dark chocolate brown, heavily white-spotted on face, neck, mantle and underparts, each body feather with a white wedge; blackish-brown cap running onto the nape; large white loral spot and white eye-ring; wings dark with a greenish-blue gloss; vent all white; tail dark with white corners and a white terminal band below. Sexes alike; juveniles barely different. Bill black, slender to stout, with white feathering at its base; iris, legs and feet black.
yebloo: Breeding: head and neck black with a purple gloss; upper mantle in dense rows of large white squares, rear back and flanks finely white-spotted; breast, belly and underwing-coverts pure white. Non-breeding: upperparts dark grey; head and hindneck dull pale grey-brown, passing to white on throat and foreneck, with a large white area round the eye. Juvenile: much as non-breeding. Bill large, pale yellow to ivory, slightly upturned — pale grey with a darker base in winter; legs and feet grey; iris wine-red.
rocbun1: Male: head pale grey, strongly marked black — a black stripe down each side of the crown, another through the eye, and a long moustachial line framing the cheek; upperparts chestnut; underparts unmarked deep buff. Female: washed-out, paler below, back grey-brown, head pattern less contrasted. Juvenile: as female but head streaked. The European race alone shows white wingbars.
grypar: Orange-brown face and throat; pale grey breast finely vermiculated black; back barred rust-brown; white belly with large chestnut horseshoe; broad rufous bars on flanks; tail rufous, central feathers mottled grey. Female: duller, back barred black, breast patch small or absent. Juvenile: yellow-brown, pale shaft-streaks, lacking face and belly marks. Bill yellow, brown or grey at the base; legs pale grey, yellowish in juveniles.
grscuc1: Dark grey above spotted white on tertials and coverts; silver-grey crest, crown and ear-coverts; white tips to flight feathers and graduated tail; face and upper breast yellowish, underparts white. Sexes alike. Juvenile: blackish above with black cap and chestnut primaries, turning sepia after the first moult. Bill black, grey at the base; legs grey; eye-ring bright orange-red at all ages.
eurnig1: Bark-patterned grey-brown, vermiculated black with buff bars and spots; pale buff hindneck collar; white moustachial line and pale throat; underparts greyish-brown barred brown. Male: white patch across three outer primaries and white tips to the two outer tail feathers. Female: those marks rust-buff, throat cinnamon. Juvenile: as female, paler. Bill blackish; iris dark brown; legs and feet brown.
monhar1: Male pale blue-grey with black wingtips; upperwing three-toned, dark grey coverts, paler secondaries, black tips; one black band along the secondaries above, two below; belly and flanks finely rufous-streaked, underwing-coverts barred rufous. Female: dark brown above with white uppertail-coverts, underparts pale yellow-brown streaked, coverts spotted. Juvenile: unspotted rufous belly and underwing-coverts. Melanistic morph regular.
twite1: Brown above streaked black, back dark; head and throat rusty-buff, throat unstreaked; underparts buff-white heavily streaked brown; pale wing bars and a dull white primary panel. Male: pink rump, and pink on breast and forehead, obscured by brown feather tips in fresh autumn plumage. Female: rump brown. Juvenile: as female but breast more heavily streaked. Bill yellow with a dark tip in winter, grey-brown in summer.
categr1: Adult all white, well feathered on the chin. Breeding: orange-buff to red-brown plumes on crown, breast and back. Sexes alike, the male marginally larger with slightly longer plumes. Juvenile: white, no plumes. Bill yellow; legs grey to yellowish; bill, legs and irides briefly bright red before pairing; juvenile bill black.
rinouz1: Male black, hooded look from the unmarked dark head, throat and nape, broken by a broad white breast crescent; wing feathers pale-edged, giving a pale wing panel in flight; belly feathers white-fringed, scaled. Female: browner, breast band duller grey. Juvenile: spotted, crescent faint or absent, but wings still paler than a Blackbird's. Bill yellow to orange with a dark tip; legs greyish brown.
reffal1: Male all sooty blue-grey, darkest about the head, with paler silvery secondaries and primaries above contrasting with dark coverts; lower belly, trousers and undertail-coverts deep rufous-red; underwing uniformly grey. Female: grey barred above, crown and whole underside bright orange, face white with black eye-mask and short moustache. Juvenile: brown above, buff below streaked dark, face as female. Male: cere, eye-ring and feet red to deep orange; bill blue-grey, dark-tipped. Juvenile: cere and feet yellow.
rennig1: Lichen-grey, barred and streaked buff, chestnut and black; underparts barred; rufous neck-collar, and throat and upper breast finely barred yellow-red; four evenly broad pale bands across the upperwing, coverts pale-tipped. Both sexes show white wing spots, white tail sides and white throat; the male's whiter.
cogwar1: Pale olive-brown above, each feather with a dark central streak; cheeks greyish; only a diffuse hint of a supercilium, faint dark streak behind the eye; underparts cream to yellow-white with a few dark spots and streaks on breast and flanks; undertail-coverts long and streaked; rump faintly spotted, concolorous with the back; tail reddish-brown, faintly barred. Upper mandible dark brown, lower yellowish-brown; legs pale yellowish to reddish-brown; iris brown.
eurwry: Bark-patterned grey-brown, finely vermiculated rufous, buff and black; broad blackish band from crown or nape down the middle of the back, and a dark lore band running well behind the eye; throat and foreneck buff barred brown; underparts creamy white with brown arrowheads becoming spots on belly; tail grey, faintly barred. Juvenile: duller, less contrasting. Bill brown to grey, sometimes greenish-tinged; legs pale brown or pale grey; iris hazel.
brant: Head, neck and primaries black, a small white crescent each side of the neck; body dark grey-brown, flanks barred black and white; white rump cut by a black wedge from the back; undertail white, tail black-sided. Pale-bellied hrota: belly pale grey against the black breast. Dark-bellied bernicla: belly as dark as the back. Bill and legs black.
eargre: Breeding: head, neck, breast and upperparts black, with a fan of ochre plumes behind the eye over the ear-coverts, not a closed triangle; flanks tawny rufous to chestnut; belly and underwing white; secondaries and inner primaries white. Non-breeding: crown, hindneck and upperparts grey-black, underparts, throat and face-sides white, the dark mark behind the eye distinct. Bill black, thin and slightly upturned; iris vivid red; legs dark greenish grey.
spocra1: Brown above, spangled with small white spots, back feathers and central coverts black; breast blue-grey; flanks dark-barred with bold white spots and pale yellow streaking; undertail plain buff to sandy. Juvenile: as adult but breast brown, not blue-grey. Chick: black down. Bill short and straight, yellow with a red base; legs green to green-yellow, toes long.
parcro2: Wings and tail dark to blackish with pale grey fringes in all plumages. Male mainly brick-red to orange, varying individually with grey-green or brown tones. Female: grey-green above, rump yellow-green, underparts pale grey washed green on breast and flanks. Juvenile: greenish yellow-grey, underparts heavily streaked blackish.
pieavo1: Pied black and white: black cap running down the nape, black lateral back, shoulders and outer primaries, the rest pure white; secondary coverts dark grey; tail white with a pale grey-brown centre. No seasonal change; sexes alike, though the female's black may look browner. Juvenile: matt brown for black, wing coverts dingy grey, back vermiculated reddish-brown. Bill black to dark grey; legs bluish grey; iris red to reddish-brown in males, hazel-brown in females.
audgul1: Head, neck, underparts and tail white; back and upperwing pale grey; primaries black with small white tips forming a string of pearls, not large mirrors; a weak white trailing edge to the secondaries. Winter: head-sides and nape freckled brown. Four years to adult plumage. Bill coral- to dark red with a black ring near the yellow or pale tip; legs grey-green to dark olive; iris dark.
lolbuz1: Pale and rufous morphs: plain creamy-rufous head with a dark eye-line and darker nape, pale streaked breast, belly, flanks and trousers rufous-brown; tail unbarred light rufous-orange; dark carpal patch and dark rump. Dark morph: head and body dark brown, tail white barred dark with a broad blackish terminal band. Juvenile: pale head, white breast, dirty-white tail.
recpoc: Male: rounded orange to red-brown head with loose crest; black breast, crop, belly and undertail-coverts; white flanks; brown back and wings; black tail. Female: pale brown, back darker, crown dark brown from eye level down, cheeks and lower neck whitish-grey, face whitish. Eclipse male: female-like but with a more contrasting head pattern. Male's bill scarlet, iris red; female's bill dark brown with a light red band at the tip, iris dark; legs brown.
ibechi2: Cleaner, warmer olive-green above with almost no brown, in autumn only on the head-side; underparts three-toned: throat and breast yellow-streaked on olive-brown, belly white, undertail-coverts bright lemon-yellow; more yellow on neck-sides and flanks than Common Chiffchaff. Vivid yellow supercilium, strongest before the eye, and a distinctly dark eye-stripe. Bill and legs paler than Common Chiffchaff's.
eurwar2: Upperparts unstreaked olive- to grey-brown; throat and breast with diffuse dark streaks; underparts dirty white, flanks olive-brown. Indistinct dirty-white supercilium, pale eye-ring. Olive-brown undertail-coverts broadly tipped whitish, giving a contrasting pattern. Juvenile: yellower below. Bill fairly dark; legs pink.
rebgoo1: Black, sharply drawn with white contour lines; breast and neck panels rusty-red, each outlined white; white flank stripe; back and belly black, upper- and undertail white. Two pale wingbars in flight. Juvenile less contrastingly marked. Feet black, webbed.
eutkne1: Sandy ground colour, cryptic, with dark streaking heaviest on neck and breast; underparts pale, at times nearly white. Sexes alike; juvenile as adult; no seasonal change. In flight very pale from below, blackish primaries with white inclusions above, striking black-and-white wing markings. Bill stout, yellow with a black tip; iris large and yellow; legs strong, yellow-green, joints swollen.
eurspo1: All white with a faint yellowish cast, head washed orange-brown. Breeding: long nape crest, spread into a fan when excited, and a yellow breast patch. Non-breeders lack crest and breast patch. Immature: black tips to the primaries. Adult bill black with a yellow tip, legs black; juvenile bill and legs pink.
cursan: Breeding adult: brick-red head and underparts, upperparts patterned grey. Non-breeding: grey above, white below with pale grey streaks, dark feather centres mottling crown and upperparts, bold white supercilium, grey-brown lores and ear-coverts. Juvenile: grey-brown above, white belly, peach-washed breast. All plumages a large white rump and a white wing-stripe. Bill black; iris dark brown; feet dark grey to black.
barwar1: Male: dark grey above with white tips to wing-coverts and tail feathers, whitish below heavily barred dark grey. Female: paler, grey-brown above, only lightly barred. Juvenile: buffy grey-brown above, pale buff-grey below, barred only on lower belly and rump, pale fringes to the wing-coverts; little else distinctive. Iris bright yellow in adult male, brown-yellow in female, dark in immature; bill blackish with a paler base; legs stout, grey-brown.
gstlar1: Sandy to greyish-brown above, finely dark-streaked on crown and upper mantle, rump plain sandy; crown rufous on some western birds. Broad dirty-white supercilium bordered below by a fine dark eye-stripe, cheeks and ear-coverts plain grey-brown. Dark patch each side of the neck. Two clear wingbars from pale-tipped coverts. Underparts unstreaked white. Sexes alike. Bill pinkish with a grey culmen.
weowar2: Male: plain grey back, head dark grey with blackish forehead, ear-coverts and mask below the eye, throat white, underparts dirty white, undertail-coverts diffusely mottled. Female: head olive-grey and much paler, back and coverts brownish-grey, flanks buff. First-winter as female but head paler grey, flanks and underparts distinctly buffier. Iris white to pale yellow in adult male, dark in female and young; legs black.
palswi3: Sooty overall but browner and paler than Common Swift, with a large white throat patch visible at a distance and a dark patch round the eye. Inner primaries and secondaries paler brown, contrasting with the rest; belly finely scaled, best seen in good light.
colfly1: Male: black above, white below, with a broad white collar, large white forehead patch, large white wing patch and pale rump; tail black, a minority with white sides. Female: grey-brown above, no collar, forehead patch small or absent, pale eye-ring, wing patch smaller. Autumn males, juveniles brown-grey and female-like. Bill black, broad-based but pointed; legs slate-grey.
goleag: Adult uniform dark to blackish brown with a golden-brown crown and nape; upper wing-coverts paler, flight feathers nearly black; tail brown, faintly darker-banded and paler at the base. Juvenile: darker, with white panels on inner primaries and outer secondaries and a white tail cut off by a broad black terminal band. Fully adult only at five to seven years. Bill dark grey; iris dark brown; legs feathered to the very strong yellow toes.
rorpar: Grass-green throughout, flight feathers dark, tail blue with the two longest feathers yellow-tipped, undertail pale yellow. Adult male: black chin drawn back as a thin line to a rose-pink nape ring, and a dark lore-stripe. Female and immature lack the ring or show a shadowy pale to dark grey one, and are duller. Upper mandible red, lower mostly black; iris pale yellow with a red orbital ring; legs greyish with dark claws.
litsti: Breeding adult: rusty upperparts finely streaked black on head and breast, white throat, strong white V on the back, white belly. Non-breeding: plain grey, difficult. Juvenile: pale crown stripes, pinkish breast, dark feather centres above, whitish or bright rufous coverts, clear white Vs; whiter about head and breast than other small waders. Bill fine and dark; legs black.
savwar1: Uniform dark reddish-brown above, sometimes faintly greenish, largely unpatterned; indistinct short buff eye-stripe, dark lores, pale brown ear-coverts. Chin, throat and belly whitish-buff, remaining underparts sandy brown, undertail the same colour as the belly. Both surfaces paler when breeding. Juvenile: yellower below. Bill slender, brown; iris brown; legs brown.
bearee1: Mostly orange-brown, cinnamon on back and flanks, whitish on throat and breast; head and nape ash-grey; tertials black edged rusty, tail rusty with white tips to the outer feathers. Male: black moustaches of elongated cheek feathers, black undertail-coverts. Female: paler, head browner, no moustaches, undertail-coverts pale buff. Juvenile: buffier, rectangular black back patch, much black in the tail. Bill bright orange-yellow, duller in the adult female.
burthr: Male: entirely blue-grey, blackish-blue, apart from darker wings; unmistakable in summer. Female and immature much plainer: dark brown above, paler brown and scaly below, grey-black with pale spots. Both sexes lack reddish outer tail feathers. Male of philippensis rufous-chestnut from mid-breast to undertail.
watpip1: Spring adult: greyish-brown above, weakly streaked darker; head grey with a broad white supercilium; underparts pale pink-buff, salmon on the breast, whitish on the belly, streaking almost absent. Non-breeding: head grey-brown, supercilium less distinct, upperparts darker and more streaked, underparts white streaked brown on breast and flanks. Young browner, more heavily streaked. Legs and toes dark grey to dark grey-brown, sometimes paler; bill dark, base of the lower mandible yellow in winter; iris dark brown.
legshr2: Male: black forehead and forecrown running back through eye and ear-coverts to the nape; crown, mantle and rump pale blue-grey; scapulars, wings and outer tail black; throat white, breast and belly flushed salmon-pink. White primary bases form a patch when perched, a crescent in flight. Female: head dark grey, upperparts browner, less pink. Juvenile: browner, back faintly barred, no pink. Bill brownish-black with a paler base to the lower mandible; iris brown; legs and feet black to dark grey-brown.
palhar1: Male: pearl-grey above, head and neck paler, white below with only head and upper breast greyish; narrow black wedge-shaped wingtips, outermost primary pale; rump grey centrally, white and faintly barred at the sides; undertail barred. Female: grey-brown above with white uppertail-coverts — a ringtail — underparts buff streaked brown, belly pale, face pattern well defined.
euptit1: Head light grey with a broad black mask through the eye; mantle and back chestnut-brown. Male: mask broader and blacker, back more rufous, boundary between brown mantle and grey nape sharp. Female duller, colours more diffuse. Juvenile in late summer and early autumn plain, without the mask: yellow-brown above, greyish-white below.
egyvul1: Adult white, wild birds usually soiled rusty or brown from mud and iron-rich soil; flight feathers black; throat feathers yellowish; head bare, wrinkled, bright yellow, sometimes orange-tinged. Sexes alike, but breeding male's facial skin deeper orange; female averages larger, 10–15% heavier. Juvenile: blackish to chocolate-brown, patched black and white, whitening moult by moult, adult at about five years. Bill black in nominate, pale or yellowish in Indian ginginianus; base yellow. Legs pink in adults, grey in juveniles. Iris reddish-brown, black in juveniles.
leskes1: Male: head slate-grey, back brick-red without black spotting, no black malar stripe; slate-grey band across the upperwing to the inner secondaries; underparts barred grey. Female and juvenile: paler, very like Common Kestrel but lacking the wing band; belly streaks more spot- or ring-shaped; underside of flight feathers pale, contrasting with the coverts; undertail paler, broad white-edged terminal band. Talons whitish-horn in all plumages, not black as in other falcons; conspicuous only at very close range.
borowl: Brown above with conspicuous pearly white spots on back, wings and scapulars; underparts whitish-grey, streaked rust-brown. Crown olive-brown with small white droplets; dull white facial disc framed dark, white eyebrows giving a startled expression. Flight feathers dark olive-brown with white spots, tail with three rows that stay separate when folded. Juvenile: dark brown, face patches, eyebrows and moustache strikingly white. Bill light yellow; iris bright yellow.
bkbplo: Breeding adult: face, throat, breast and flanks black; mantle boldly spangled black and white, running up nape and crown; white supercilium joining on the forehead and running behind the ear-coverts into white patches at the breast sides. Female: black duller, greyer, flecked white. Winter and juvenile: plain grey above, breast grey-speckled, belly white; juvenile back feathers blacker with creamy edges. Bill short, heavy, black to grey-black in all plumages; legs grey to grey-black; eyes dark.
leseag1: Adult brown; body, head and wing-coverts warm pale brown, contrasting with uniformly dark grey-brown flight and tail feathers. Whitish bases to the inner primaries make a pale patch on the upperwing; upper tail-coverts broadly white-edged, adults keeping a white V on the rump. Juvenile: less wing contrast, prominent white spots on the remiges, cream neck patch, no covert spotting. Iris orange-yellow; cere and toes yellow; bill black with a grey base.
eursco1: Bark-coloured, predominantly grey-brown, from grey to chestnut, with variable white flecking; face, underparts and shoulder line paler. Bold black longitudinal streaks below; white spots on back and forehead; shoulder bands white. Iris yellow-orange.
ettwoo1: Black and white, no red or pink anywhere; dark-looking. Dark cheeks, yellowish malar stripe, white supercilium running V-shaped into the nape, meeting the white black-barred back or ending on the black upper back in alpinus. Wing coverts black, no white shoulder patch; primaries and outer tail feathers barred, flanks white barred black. Male: crown yellow, female black-grey, juvenile yellow.
easwar1: Male: head and mantle lead-grey; throat and breast intense cinnamon to brick-red, cut off by a broad white malar streak and contrasting with the paler belly. Female: head paler grey, back grey-olive, throat and flanks washed pink, white below. First-winter: olive-brown above, white below. Both sexes: a white pointed wedge on the second-outermost tail feather — hard to see, diagnostic. Male: eye-ring and orbital ring brick-red, iris dark; legs brown-pink; bill beige, dark on tip and culmen. Female: eye-ring whitish.
rebfly: Head and upperparts dull dark brown, unmarked. Male: throat orange-red, diffuse against the buff-white breast, sharply bordered by slate-grey neck sides, head and nape. Female: no red throat, no grey, whitish below with a yellowish flank wash. Tail black with white bases to the outer feathers, wheatear-like; upper tail-coverts paler than the tail. Noticeable white orbital ring in all plumages. Bill black with a pale pinkish base to the lower mandible, extensive and obvious from below; eye large and dark.
blasto1: Black with a purple-green metallic sheen over head, neck, breast, back and upperwing; lower breast, belly, axillaries and undertail-coverts white, showing as a white triangle in the armpit. Breast feathers long and shaggy, forming a courtship ruff. In strong sun the upperwing can look pale. Juvenile: browner, duller, green-black without sheen, pale tips to scapulars and coverts. Adult: bill and legs bright red when breeding, brownish to dull dark red otherwise; bare eye-skin red; iris brown. Juvenile: legs and bill grey-green.
purher1: Darker and more reddish-brown than Grey Heron, adults also darker grey on the back. Forehead and crown black, a dark stripe down the hindneck ending in a slender dangling crest. Head and neck sides buff-chestnut with dark lines down each side; mantle oily brown; breast chestnut-brown, belly and undertail-coverts black. First-winter: upperparts, coverts, neck and head ochre-brown, neck streaks indistinct. Bill long, straight, powerful, brownish-yellow and brighter when breeding, culmen dark, upper mandible base pale; iris yellow; legs brown in front, yellowish behind.
wooduc: Male: head and neck black glossed green and violet, nape drawn out into a crest, two white lines each side — from the bill base and from behind the eye; white throat notching up the cheek; breast purple with white spots; flanks red-violet, orange-streaked; belly white; speculum blue-green, white-edged behind. Female: olive-brown and grey, white eye-ring, whitish throat, white belly. Male: iris red, bill reddish with a black tip and pale yellow stripe below, legs and feet orange-yellow. Female: bill dark grey, legs yellowish.
caster1: White head with a black cap, white neck, belly and tail; upperwing and back pale grey; underwing pale with dark primaries, so the wingtips look black from below and can show a dark triangular wedge from above. Winter: cap retained, but the forehead streaked white. Juvenile: crown, wings, back and tail mottled grey-brown. Bill thick, coral to orange-red with a black tip or broad dark subterminal band, duller orange and shorter in juveniles; legs black to dark brown.
bkewhe2: Breeding male: forehead, crown and mantle white or nearly white; wings blacker than Northern Wheatear's; back, rump and most of the tail white, the black terminal band broader at the corners; black mask from ear-coverts to just above the bill base. Black-throated morph, whole face black, commoner than the white-throated. Female: grey-brown, colder-toned and duller, white lower back.
spaeag1: Overall darker than either Golden or Eastern Imperial Eagle: a rich blackish-brown running from the throat right down to the belly. Nape and hindneck contrastingly pale beige. Broad white band on the shoulder and leading edge of the wing, even more pronounced than in Eastern Imperial; shoulders and bend of wing conspicuously white-marked.
bkewhe1: Breeding male: forehead and forecrown white, rest of crown, nape and upper mantle ochre-buff, bleaching near-white by July; lower back and rump white; lores and ear-coverts black. Wings uniformly black; central tail feathers black, the rest white with a black terminal band widening outwards. Breast yellow-buff, belly whitish. Throat white or black by morph. Female: browner, white lower back.
litbit1: Male: crown, nape, back, scapulars and tail black, faintly green-sheened; a large pinkish-buff oval panel on the inner wing-coverts contrasts with the otherwise black wing; underwing wholly whitish; underparts pale buff. Female: duller, upperparts brownish-black with paler feather margins, underparts streaked dark buff and brown, wing panel less obvious and browner. Juvenile: duller, more rufous, heavily streaked above and below.
boneag2: Adult: upperparts and crown uniform blackish-brown, with a whitish patch in the middle of the back. Underbody and lesser underwing-coverts white with variable black streaking, contrasting sharply with the uniformly black median and greater underwing-coverts. Tail grey above, white below, finely barred with a broad dark subterminal band. Juvenile: underparts and underwing-coverts yellow-brown, tail closely barred, no black terminal band.
ruewar1: Male: forehead, head and throat black, split by a clean white malar streak; back grey, rump paler grey, underparts pale grey with a paler wash down the centre. Wing feathers black with broad pale fringes, secondaries and tertials white-edged; tail black, outer feathers white-edged. Female: head lead-grey, forehead black-speckled, throat pale and dark-spotted, back grey with a brown tinge. Male: broad, bright red eye-ring, iris reddish-brown; legs ochre-brown; lower mandible pale beige. Female: eye-ring narrow and dark red within a thin white orbital ring.
pygcor2: Dark throughout, black with dark-green and brown gloss; head dark red-brown. Breeding adult: white spots on head and neck. Non-breeding: no white spots, breast paler and brown-toned. Juvenile: duller and browner.
eueowl1: Upperparts dark brown, coarsely blotched and barred black; breast heavily black-streaked on a yellow-brown ground; belly rusty-buff with fine black streaks; underparts and underwing paler than the back; black-and-white band across the wing; throat white, shown only when calling. Juvenile: pale grey down, head still downy, tufts small. Iris orange-yellow; tarsus and claws heavy.
eaowar1: Upperparts plain grey-brown with an olive tinge, back and uppertail-coverts a shade yellower-brown; below whitish, breast-sides and flanks warm greyish-buff; undertail-coverts cream-white; narrow cream supercilium from bill-base to eye, dark lores, thin pale eye-ring; faint pale wing panel; tail dark grey-brown with grey-white tips and edges; never rufous on the rump. Juvenile: buffier belly. Bill dark horn above, pale pink-yellow to yellow-brown below; legs dark grey-brown with a pinkish cast.
citwag: Breeding male: head bright lemon-yellow, yellow continuing over the underparts and whitening to white undertail-coverts; black band about 1 cm wide across the nape onto the upper breast-sides; mantle mid-grey, rump dark grey; white on the remiges; two outer tail-feather pairs mostly white. Winter: yellow diluted white, head brownish with yellowish supercilium. Female: washed-out winter male. Bill slender, blackish, sometimes paler grey to flesh at the base below; feet and legs blackish; iris dark brown, grey-brown in younger birds.
brbsan: Breeding adult: upperparts dark, boldly patterned with narrow pale fringes forming a double V down the mantle; pale crown-stripe and a distinctive split supercilium forking before the eye; white below, breast with blackish arrowhead marks reaching the flanks. Winter: much paler grey above, white below, head pattern kept. Juvenile: paler and cleaner; white flanks and belly diagnostic. Bill dark brown.
blhbun1: Breeding male: hood black; upperparts and rump chestnut, unstreaked; underparts bright unstreaked yellow with a yellow breast band; no white in the tail. Autumn male after partial moult: head brown, like the female. Female: head grey-brown, upperparts duller olive-brown, underparts paler but unstreaked. Juvenile: as female, vent yellow; first-year male grey-crowned with chestnut and grey patches on the back. Bill conical, pale grey.
tunswa: Adult all white; head and neck may take a golden or rusty hue in iron-rich water. Immature: white mixed with dull grey, head and upper neck often wholly light grey; first-summer already largely white, adult plumage in the second winter. Downy young silvery grey above, white below. Bill mostly black with a thin salmon-pink mouthline and yellow at the base, extensive in bewickii, nearly absent in columbianus; feet black; iris dark brown.
isawhe1: Sexes alike; male averages blacker lores.
