Upperparts pale sandy brown, isabelline-tinged; rump and uppertail-coverts white; tail with broad black terminal band, black central feathers and large white base; creamy-white supercilium, pale brown ear-coverts; throat pale buff, breast sandy buff, belly creamy white; black alula contrasting with the pale wing. Juvenile: grey-brown above with yellowish-white fringes and spots. Bill, legs and feet black; iris brown.
ortbun1: Male: head, neck and breast dull grey-green; yellow throat, curved yellow submoustachial stripe and yellow-white orbital ring contrast strongly; mantle rust-brown, boldly blackish-streaked; belly cinnamon-brown; tertial fringes red-brown, broadest in the middle. Female: hood lacking or barely hinted, colours paler, crown, throat-sides and breast finely dark-streaked. Juvenile: adult tones but dulled and indistinct.
horlar: Face pattern striking black and yellow (black and white in Asian and north-west arctic birds); upperparts mainly brown-grey, variably rufous-toned by subspecies; underparts pale; tail mostly black except the central feathers, contrasting strongly with the paler body, especially in flight. Female: horns shorter, mask paler and less contrasting. Southern European penicillata greyer above, white replacing the yellow. Bill short and dark; legs dark grey.
bkskit1: Predominantly white to pale grey with black shoulder patches, black wingtips and a black eye-stripe; black on the underside of the primaries and on part of the upperwing-coverts; plumage velvety; sexes alike. Juvenile: crown browner, breast rust-coloured. Eyes bright red, large and forward-facing under a shading bony shelf; legs orange-yellow.
whwter: Breeding adult: head, neck, breast and belly black, back very dark grey, rump white, tail pale grey to whitish; upperwing largely white, underwing-coverts and axillaries black; face tinged yellowish. Female duller. Winter: black replaced by white and pale grey, crown grey-streaked, dark ear-patch, broad white collar. Juvenile: dark brown saddle isolated by white collar and pale grey rump. Bill black and stubby; legs red, longer than Black Tern's.
eurrol1: Head, neck and whole underparts turquoise, pale blue in sun and turquoise-green in shade; forehead and chin whitish-grey; upper back and scapulars rusty cinnamon; lower back violet-blue, uppertail-coverts ultramarine; central tail feathers dark olive-green, the rest turquoise-azure with darker bases, outermost slightly elongated and dark-edged; flight-feather ends blue-black. Female paler overall; juvenile a drabber adult. Small bare black area behind the eye.
tawpip1: Adult upperparts plain pale sandy grey-brown; median coverts contrastingly darker with broad pale tips, showing on a perched fresh bird as five dark squares; cream supercilium ending over the ear-coverts, blackish lores, white throat; underparts pale and unstreaked but for a few fine streaks at the breast-sides; outer tail feathers cream-tipped. Juvenile: heavily dark-streaked above, spotted on the breast. Bill grey-brown and slender, lower mandible pale at the base; legs pale brown to light pink.
grebus1: Head and neck pale ash-grey; on the male the neck is white above, shading to rust-brown below. Upperparts, back and scapulars barred rust-brown and black; secondaries white with black-brown tips; underparts pale grey. Male's rust tones far more intense than female's; older males carry long whisker-like feathers from each side of the bill-base, hanging back and down; female lacks these.
ferduc: Male rich dark chestnut on head, breast and flanks, back darker; undertail-coverts brilliant white, sharply cut off against the black-brown lower back; white belly patch and white underwing show in flight, with a clear white wingbar. Female similar but duller and browner, with less contrast between back and body. Non-breeding male keeps the same pattern, only less bright. Male's iris white to yellow, female's dark brown; bill long, dark grey to blue-black with a black nail and often a paler tip.
litbus1: Breeding male: head and throat lead-grey; neck deep black with two white bands, one above and one below; upperparts sandy brown with dark markings, underparts white. Female and non-breeding male lack the neck pattern, sandy above with black spots and more vermiculated, white on breast and belly; female darker below than male. Juvenile like female.
comwax: Grey-brown throughout, finely barred wavy dark brown; broad scarlet stripe through the eye; cheeks and throat whitish; belly often flushed pink with a reddish stripe down the centre, varying by subspecies; rump brown, tail and vent dark. Female: paler, less red on the belly. Juvenile: duller, little or no red below, barring fainter. Bill sealing-wax red in the adult, blackish to brown-black in the juvenile.
grefla3: Adult mostly pinkish-white; wing-coverts red, primaries and secondaries black. Subadult paler with dark legs; adults feeding chicks also pale but keeping bright pink legs. Chick in short dense grey down, light grey above and whitish below, lores bare; a second, darker grey down at about four weeks. Colour comes from carotenoids in the food. Bill pink with a sharply defined, restricted black tip; legs entirely pink; orbital ring pink.
bcnher: Adult: crown, nape-crest, back and scapulars black; forehead and face white; wings and rest of body ash-grey; one to eight long slender white nape plumes, raised in greeting and courtship. Male slightly larger, with a longer crest in the breeding season. Immature: dull grey-brown head, wings and back with numerous pale teardrop spots, underparts paler and brown-streaked. Iris red, yellow to amber in young birds; bill black; legs short and pale yellow-green, turning bright salmon-pink with blue lores briefly in courtship.
arcwar1: Upperparts greyish-green to olive-brown, underparts off-white with some small streaks on the breast; long, clear supercilium and dark eye-stripe; a single narrow white wingbar. Bill heavy, with a dark tip to the lower mandible.
whiter2: Summer adult: black cap, white cheeks; dark grey above and below, mantle silvery-grey; rump pale grey all year. Winter: forehead white, body much paler grey; black ear-coverts joined to blackish hindcrown as a C-shaped band, mottled white above; neck sides white, collar ill-defined. Juvenile: back dark brown with broad buff edges, ginger and scaly. Bill and legs red in the summer adult.
gloibi: Breeding adult: reddish-brown to deep purple body, wings strongly iridescent bottle-green, bronze or purple with the light; narrow white facial band above and below the bill. Non-breeding and juvenile: duller and dull brown, dark head and neck finely streaked and spotted white, juvenile paler brown below. Sexes alike. Bill brownish, grey-based, orange-tipped, pinker when not breeding; facial skin dark, bordered blue-grey to cobalt blue when breeding; legs red-brown.
alpswi1: Upperparts olive-brown, wing-tips looking blacker. Underside diagnostic: white throat and whole fore-belly cut by a sharply defined dark breast-band, the oval white belly patch ringed by olive-brown flanks and undertail-coverts. Sexes alike; throat patch often hard to see. Races vary from pale grey-brown to blackish. Bill black; iris brown-black; feet black in adults, flesh-coloured in juveniles, claws black.
blawhe1: Male: all black, glossy and intense after the moult, duller when breeding; rump, undertail-coverts and tail white, the tail with a bold black inverted T; flight feathers pale-fringed. Female: as male but duller, brownish-black — usually only told in direct comparison.
rebcho1: Adult velvet-black, glossed green on the body, the metallic sheen varying between populations; sexes alike in colour. Juvenile less glossy. Legs lack the scaling shown by other corvids; nasal bristles very short, barely covering the nostrils. Bill and legs red in adults; juvenile has an orange to brown-yellow bill and pink legs until its first autumn.
rocnut1: Pale-looking overall; juveniles duller than the adults. No white on the underside of the tail.
rtrthr1: Summer male unmistakable: blue-grey head, orange-red breast and underparts, white back, dark brown wings, rufous outer tail feathers. Female and immature much plainer — dark brown scaly above, paler scaly orange-buff below, tail rufous as in the male. Juvenile more spotted than the female. Both sexes show a dark brown tail centre flanked by rufous.
refblu1: Male: deep blue above, brighter cobalt on rump, tail sides, shoulder and crown sides, darkest on cheeks and neck sides; white throat, creamy-white underparts, bright orange flanks; white streak over forehead and eye. Female and immature male: olive-brown above with blue rump and tail, dusky breast, whitish throat and eye-ring, orange flanks. Juvenile spotted, like a young robin. Bill small, thin and black; legs slender and black.
kenplo1: Grey-brown to sandy above, white below, with a white hind-collar and whitish supercilium. Summer male: black frontal bar, black stripe through the eye, black ear-coverts, rufous crown and nape, and two dark breast-side patches forming a broken collar. Female paler, without the black and rufous. In flight: white wingbar, white rump, black tail with white sides. Bill black, short and fine; eye black; legs dark to black in summer, grey in winter and in juveniles.
purswa: Dark blue plumage shimmering violet-purple; undertail-coverts white. Juvenile duller, grey with grey-white feathering down the centre of the underparts. Bill, frontal shield and legs bright red, the shield paler in winter; juvenile bill and legs grey-pink.
gubter2: Summer adult: black cap from forehead to nape, pale grey upperparts to the tail, white underparts. Winter: cap lost, forehead white, back a whiter grey, and a dark patch through the eye. Juvenile: much like the winter adult but with a fainter mask and often brown-fringed feathers. Bill black, short and thick; legs black.
boowar1: Plain greyish-brown above, beige-brown when fresh, whitish below with rust-buff flanks; short pale supercilium and a clearer dark eye-stripe, sometimes a hint of a dark lateral crown-stripe; narrow white edge to the outer tail feather, hard to see. Juvenile olive-brown with an ochre cast, yellowish-brown on head and underparts. Bill short, dark above with a distinct dark tip and pale brown-pink base; legs brownish-pink, toes darker grey.
compea: Male: metallic blue crown with a fan-shaped crest of bare shafts tipped blue-green; bare white stripe above and white crescent below the eye; neck and breast purple-blue, mantle scaly bronze-green, wing with chestnut primaries and black secondaries, belly blackish; train of bronze-green upper tail-coverts bearing purple-black, blue and copper eye-spots. Female mostly brown-grey, no train.
lwfgoo: Like Greater White-fronted but smaller and darker, especially on the head; white facial blaze runs up over the forehead, ending between the eyes; belly crossed by broad black bars, weaker than in Greater White-fronted; upper wing-coverts mouse-coloured. Downy young brown above, whitish below, cream face and neck, dark lores, red-brown forehead. Orbital ring bright yellow, yellow-green in juveniles until the moult of their first November; legs bright orange.
colpra: Dull mid-brown above and on head, chin and fore-breast; upper wing-coverts brown against darker flight feathers; white trailing edge to the wing; belly, rump and uppertail-coverts white, tail black; underwing chestnut but often looking wholly dark. White streak under the large black eye. Summer: cream-yellow throat ringed black. Winter: ring lost. Juvenile scaly, greyer, with a dark breast-band. Bill short and dark, red at the base in summer adults; eye large and black.
eurdot: All plumages: broad whitish supercilia meeting in a V on the nape, and a pale breast-band. Summer adult unmistakable; black crown, streaked head, slate-grey neck and breast above the white line, chestnut breast to black belly, white vent, warm brown pale-edged back; female brighter. Winter and juvenile washed out, buff-yellow below, grey vermiculated above, juvenile white-fringed. Bill short and black to grey-black; legs yellow to green-yellow.
tersan: Grey back, face and breast in all plumages; belly whitish; pale supercilium more or less distinct. Breeding birds add black lengthwise stripes on the scapulars. Bill black with a yellowish base, dull red at the base when breeding; legs short, yellow to orange.
squher1: On the ground dull ochre-yellow-brown and inconspicuous; in flight strikingly white, wings and tail white. Breeding adult: back beige-brown with a faint purple sheen, neck and flanks unstreaked cream-yellow, head streaked, nape feathers elongated. Non-breeding: head, neck and flanks clearly streaked grey, nape plumes short, mantle dull ochre-brown. Juvenile darker and more heavily streaked. Breeding: bill green-blue with black tip, legs coral-red, bare eye skin bright green. Non-breeding: bill and legs yellow-green, bill dark-tipped, eye skin yellow.
somtit3: Cap and nape sooty brownish-black in the male, more chocolate-brown in the female, running further down the sides of the head than in other tits; the large black bib squeezes the off-white cheek to a narrow wedge. Rest of upperparts grey-brown; underparts dull whitish with greyish-brown flanks. Juvenile duller and browner.
musduc: Predominantly black with large white wing patches; back and wing feathers iridescent and glossy in the male, drabber in the female. Male has a short erectile nape crest and a bare face; female smaller, face feathered. Juvenile duller, little or no white on the wing. Domestic birds far more variable, often extensively white. Bill black speckled pink; male with a blackish or dark red knob at the bill base matching the bare face skin; eyes yellow-brown; legs blackish.
blbsan1: Male: head, neck and breast grey; throat chestnut with a black spot; upperparts golden-brown with darker markings, belly black; black band across the buff breast and a thin black border round the lower breast. Female: browner and more finely marked above, head and neck more strongly streaked; underparts and breast band as male.
whwcro: Male: forehead, crown, nape and upperparts bright raspberry-red, brighter and pinker than other crossbills; scapulars black to blackish-brown edged pink; uppertail-coverts black fringed white. Two broad white wing-bars, the lower broadest inwards, the upper falling away obliquely, and broad sharply defined white tertial tips. Female: head and upperparts greenish-yellow, no pink. Juvenile: grey below, heavily streaked, wing-bars much narrower.
litcra1: Male: upperparts brown with blackish and white markings; face and underparts blue-grey, flanks only faintly barred. Female: underparts buff, grey confined to the face. Juvenile: as female but face and breast white. Undertail short and barred black and white. Downy chick black. Bill short and straight, yellow to olive-green with a red base; legs green, toes long.
subwar8: Male: upperparts lead-grey, white moustachial stripe, underparts red — but paler than Western Subalpine, salmon or old rose rather than brick-red. Female: paler than the male, back brown-grey, only a faint red tone below, white eye-ring. Juvenile all but identical to Western Subalpine.
laudov1: Head and underparts pinkish, head and neck tinged lilac, shading buff on the lower belly; chequered rufous and grey patch of split feathers on the neck sides; upperparts brownish with a blue-grey band along the wing; outer tail feathers tipped white. Sexes alike in the field; young lack the chequered neck patch. Arid-zone birds paler. Legs red.
weowar1: Upperparts plain pale brown to isabelline, warmer and ochre on the rump; wing uniform, feathers without pale fringes, only the alula darker; tail tips brownish-white and very indistinct. Underparts whitish, washed yellow-brown on breast sides and flanks. Head plain — short pale supercilium from bill to eye running into a faint eye-ring, no eye-stripe. Young buffer on the belly. Bill dark grey to brown above, dull yellowish-brown below; iris dark brown; legs and feet grey-brown to greyish flesh.
chukar: Back light brown, breast grey, belly buff, flanks streaked rufous; face white with a sharply defined black gorget, throat patch cream to yellowish; black band round the eyes enclosing a red-brown ear patch, broad diffuse grey-white supercilium; crown wine-red, ash-grey at sides and hindneck, forehead black; rump and lower back ash-grey; outer tail feathers rufous. Sexes alike. Bill coral red; eye cere coral red; legs coral red.
cockat: Normal grey: mainly grey with prominent white flashes along the outer edge of each wing; round orange ear patch in both sexes. Male: face yellow or white, cheek patch vivid, tail underside plain. Female: face grey, cheek patch muted, tail underside barred yellow and black, plumage paler. Juvenile like the female. Many bred colour varieties differ widely.
crebun2: Breeding male: head bright blue-grey, not olive; throat and moustachial stripe cinnamon-orange, not yellow; upperparts brown and heavily streaked, rump unstreaked warm rust-brown; underparts rusty orange; eye-ring white, not yellow. Female: duller and more heavily streaked, but throat and moustache still cinnamon. In autumn the bright colours are partly veiled. Juvenile very hard to tell from Ortolan. Bill stout, pink to reddish-pink.
afbtit2: Forehead and supercilium white to mid-nape, framing a deep glossy blue crown blackening on the neck; blackish lores and eye-stripe joined across the blue-grey nape, with black chin and collar enclosing white cheeks; back, rump and coverts blue-grey; underparts deep yellow with a black belly stripe. Sexes alike. Juvenile: supercilium, nape and ear-coverts yellow, upperparts greenish-blue, belly stripe usually absent. Bill small and pointed, slate-grey to black with paler cutting edges; iris dark brown to black; legs dark grey.
medshe1: Upperparts blackish brown, the outer wing darkest, the whole upperside more brown-grey than Manx's blackish; underparts sharply cut off and mainly plain white; dark wingtips, dark tail band and a dark diagonal band across the underwing-coverts; flanks, axillaries, undertail and underwing-coverts variably browner; underwing less contrasting than Manx, the primaries grey rather than black.
pitsan1: Breeding male: crown, neck, back and underwing-coverts yellowish-green with dull yellow shoulder spots; cheeks yellow, narrow black line from bill through eye to nape; black throat patch; chestnut breast-band edged black cuts the white belly from the green neck; rump and tail barred black and brownish-yellow. Non-breeding: crown and upperparts barred, throat whitish. Female: duller, throat white, extra black neck-band. Bill slate-grey; iris brown; legs feathered dull white.
slbgul1: Adult: body pale grey, head and breast white — no dark hood in any season; primaries black-tipped; in summer the breast is faintly pink, the neck, underbody and tail flushed pink. First-year: upperparts grey, underparts white, grey mottling on crown and nape, black terminal tail band and dark areas in the wing. Two years to maturity. Bill dark red, thin and fine; legs dark red; iris yellow. Juvenile bill yellow-orange, legs yellow.
whtrob3: Breeding male: upperparts lead-grey to blue-grey, face black, white supercilium and a white throat running as a triangle from the bill base to the breast; underparts orange, vent white; tail black above. Female: plainer, grey-brown above with a white supercilium; underparts creamy, orange on the lower breast and flanks, upper breast grey-brown, throat patch faint; tail black above. Bill strong and black.
snogoo: Two morphs. White morph: all white but for black primaries and grey primary coverts. Blue morph: head, upper neck and tail tip white, the rest bluish grey-brown; immature blue drab slate-grey with little or no white on head, neck or belly. Intermediates occur; juveniles generally greyish. Head often stained rusty brown by minerals where they feed. Bill pink to orange-pink with black tomia, giving a black grin patch; feet and legs rose-red; all duller in immatures.
eaowar2: Male: head dark grey to black as a neatly demarcated cap, with a black eye-mask; back and upperwing grey; throat white, breast dirty white, flanks faintly buff; undertail-coverts always dark in the centre, giving a blotched look. Female and immature: head paler, underparts reddish, back grey with a brownish tinge. Legs black; iris white in adults, dark in young birds; bill long, in males with more clearly marked blue-white at the base.
grseag1: Adult almost uniform dark to blackish brown, sometimes purplish and glossy; upperwing-coverts often a shade paler; two contrasts only — a pale beak and a narrow white U above the tail, usually hidden at rest; flight and tail feathers slightly paler brown-grey. Rare pale fulvescens morph: head, body and all coverts pale beige to gold. Juvenile white-spotted on the wings. Beak pale yellow, contrasting.
whsbul1: Head near-black as a dark face mask, contrasting sharply with grey-brown breast and mantle; whitish eye-ring — the spectacles; undertail-coverts lemon-yellow; long tail feathers finely edged white. Sexes alike. Juvenile: hood browner, eye-ring less obvious.
rintea1: Drake: back rich chestnut, flanks pale grey, breast salmon speckled black, a black band from the top of the head down the nape. Female: back olive-brown, head blotched and streaked white, breast and belly pale with fine pencilled barring. Both sexes: dark tail, contrasting pale rump, distinctive white patch on the wing. Same plumage all year; no eclipse. Bill grey; legs and feet pink in both sexes.
finwhe1: Summer male: white crown, back and belly against black face, throat and wings; rump and tail white with an inverted black T, the terminal band evenly wide; black of the throat runs down into the wing; in flight the black flight feathers look fairly pale. Female: brown-grey above, dirty white below; wing-coverts low in contrast; tail pattern as the male.
alepar2: Largely green; light blue-grey sheen on cheeks and nape; abdomen yellow-green; red shoulder patch, on a perched bird a red-brown block on the inner forewing. Uppertail green shading to blue, tipped yellow; undertail yellow. Male: black stripe across the lower cheek and a pink nape band. Female: both lacking. Juvenile: as female but shorter-tailed. Bill massive, red with yellow tips.
rutscr1: Upperparts rich brownish chestnut, rump and uppertail-coverts more rufous; broad creamy-white curved supercilium from nostrils to behind eye, dark brown line through lores and eye; ear-coverts pale brown. Underparts buffish white, chin, central belly and undertail-coverts palest. Secondaries white-tipped. Tail rufous-chestnut, outer feathers broadly black-banded and white-tipped. Juvenile: paler sandy-brown. Western birds paler, warmer above. Iris and bill brown, lower mandible grey at the base; legs and feet pale brown.
spwlap1: Forehead, crown and crest black; nape white, running down the neck side below the eye to the bill base and in broad wedges onto the breast sides, split by a broad black chin-to-breast stripe. Breast and belly black, vent and undertail-coverts sharply white. Mantle to rump pale brown; coverts brown white-tipped or all white; tail black, white-based. Bill blackish; legs brownish-black; iris strong red to red-brown.
spewar2: Male: head grey with black lores and fore-cheek and black ear-coverts, throat white, eye-ring white; back grey-brown; breast dark brown-pink, darker than whitethroat's; wings uniformly rusty-brown. Female: head browner than female whitethroat, the rusty-brown on the wing broad. Immatures very like whitethroat and western subalpine warbler — hard in the field. Legs pale yellowish-pink.
yebcho1: Glossy black throughout. Sexes alike, the male averaging slightly larger. Juvenile: duller, with a dull yellow bill and brownish legs. Bill short and yellow; legs and toes red; iris dark brown.
grgowl: Low-contrast grey-brown. Facial disc near-circular, grey-white, up to nine concentric dark rings; two white crescents about the small yellow eyes widen beside the bill into a bold X, with a black median line above and black beard below; white collar or bow-tie beneath. Upperparts grey, dark-streaked, pale-barred; underparts paler, streaked blackish-brown. Tail five- or six-banded. Female larger and whiter below. Bill yellow; iris yellow, ringed darker.
masshr1: Male: deep black above; crown and nape black, forehead, cheeks, supercilium and neck sides white, split by a narrow black eye-stripe; white scapular patch and white primary bases; outer tail feathers white; underparts white, orange on flanks and breast. Female: duller, brownish-black above, white patches smaller and buff-tinged. Juvenile: grey-brown, barred head to rump, forehead pale grey, underparts barred off-white. Bill black; legs and toes slate-grey to black; iris brown.
afrcha1: Male: head blue-grey with a small black patch on the forehead; mantle moss-green; wings black with two bold white stripes and white-edged tertials and secondaries; tail blue-grey, white-sided; throat, breast and belly pale pink, whitening on lower belly and undertail. Winter male duller, head grey-brown, mantle brownish-green. Female and juvenile: greyish brown, wings striped dark brown and white, underparts paler. Bill silvery blue-grey with a black tip; legs dark pinkish-brown, brown in female and juvenile.
alpacc1: Head and breast grey; throat finely vermiculated black and white, showing frontally as a narrow white bar; flanks and underparts streaked red-brown; upperparts streaked black, grey and brown. Wing-coverts black, edged in fresh autumn plumage by two white bars; tail tip whitish. Sexes alike. Juvenile: head browner, throat plain grey, underparts spotted brownish. Bill sharp and black with a yellow-orange base.
impeag1: Adult almost uniformly blackish-brown; crown and nape pale beige to golden; clear white spots on the scapulars. Upper- and underwing-coverts dark, contrasting only weakly with slightly paler, uniform dark grey flight feathers. Tail silvery grey and finely dark-barred at the base, with a broad black subterminal band and a narrow white tip.
budger: Body light green; head and upper back finely barred black on yellow, broadening into crossbars on the coverts; forehead, eye-region, throat and fore-cheek yellow; iridescent blue-violet cheek patches and a row of black round throat spots. Tail cobalt to greenish-blue, outer feathers with central yellow flashes; flight feathers greenish-black, coverts black fringed yellow. Juvenile: duller, barring reaching forehead and cere. Bill olive-grey; legs and feet blue-grey; cere blue in males, brown, beige, white or pale blue in females.
semfly1: Breeding male: black above, white below; large white forehead patch; white half-collar reaching further back than pied's; large white wing patch and white primary bases; white-tipped median coverts, unique in both sexes; most white of the three at the tail base; rump often pale grey. Female, non-breeding male and juvenile: black replaced by pale brown, hard to separate from collared. Bill black.
pecsan: Crown dark brown streaked black; ear-coverts red-brown against paler streaked cheeks; throat white. Neck and breast pale brownish, densely dark-streaked into a broad band cut off sharply against the white underparts. Mantle and back dark with broad chestnut fringes, looking scaly; brownest in summer male, greyest in winter; breeding male blacker-breasted, spotted white. Juvenile: brighter rufous above, white mantle stripes. Bill olive with a darker tip; legs yellowish; iris dark brown.
grwpel1: White throughout, flushed pink when freshly moulted in October, the flush soon fading. At the start of breeding the crown feathers lengthen into a crest up to 14 cm, shorter in the female, its base tapering wedge-like onto the forehead; the eye region is bare. Bill pink and yellow, bluish grey on culmen and base, nail red; pouch pale to yolk-yellow, chrome-yellow before breeding; iris red- to dark brown.
cypwhe1: Crown and nape white, in fresh autumn plumage blackish-brown with small white spots, wearing whiter. Lores, face, throat, upper breast, mantle, back, scapulars and wings black, slightly glossy; breast beige. Tail black and white in the usual wheatear pattern but with a broad black terminal band, the white rump not reaching far up the back. Sexes essentially alike.
monpar1: Upperparts bright green; forehead, throat and breast pale grey with darker scalloping; rest of the underparts pale green to yellow; flight feathers dark blue, the wing blue-toned; tail green. Sexes look alike — the slight difference in crown and covert colour is invisible to the eye. Bill orange.
marsan: Breeding: upperparts cream to pink-grey or greyish brown, boldly spotted and vermiculated black; breast densely black-spotted, flanks with black chevrons; forehead, cheeks and supercilium whitish, indistinctly streaked. Winter: grey above, white below, head and neck whitish. Juvenile: upperparts brown with cream spots. A diffuse white supercilium and white feathering round the bill base in all plumages. Legs long, thin and yellowish.
whtkin2: Back, wings and tail bright blue to blue-green; head, shoulders, flanks and lower belly chestnut; throat and upper breast chalk-white. In flight a sky-blue carpal patch above and a large white panel below, wing tips black. Sexes alike; juvenile a duller version of the adult. Bill and legs coral-red.
lammer1: Adult: slate to grey-black above with pale shafts; head, neck and underparts white to sandy-beige or rusty red, got by dust-bathing; creamy forehead cut by a black band across lores and eyes, running into black chin bristles — the beard. Underwing grey-brown, coverts very dark. Juvenile: grey-black with dark head, blunter wingtip, shorter tail; adult after five to seven years. Bill strong and pale; iris yellow, ringed by a red sclera that brightens as the bird grows excited.
redava: Breeding male: deep red on face, neck sides and underparts, flanks flecked white; lores dark; back and scapulars brownish red, white-spotted; wings blackish-brown, coverts and tertials white-tipped; rump and uppertail-coverts red, spotted pink to white; lower belly and undertail-coverts blackish, tail white-tipped below. Female and non-breeding male: brown above, beige below, orange on flanks, keeping red bill and red rump. Bill bright red in all adult plumages, with a dark line along the upper mandible; iris red, red-brown or orange; feet flesh to brownish.
soclap1: Breeding adult: black crown and lores framed above and below by a strong white supercilium; upper neck warm sandy; mantle, scapulars and breast grey-brown with a pinkish-beige tone; belly black grading to dark chestnut at the vent; undertail-coverts white. Winter: head pattern duller, upperparts browner, belly white. Juvenile: scaly above, breast diffusely streaked, white supercilium still bold. Bill short and black; legs long and black, dark grey in some birds.
rossta2: Male: body matt pink, contrasting glossy black head, wings and tail; crest reaching the nape, glossed metallic green like the wings. Female: duller, crest shorter, wings browner, pink and black not sharply divided. Winter: crest shorter and black feathers pale-fringed, plumage dull until the fringes wear. Juvenile: paler than young Starling, dark wings against a pale body and pale rump. Bill and legs pale orange; juvenile bill short, yellow, yellowish at the base.
cacgoo1: Black head and neck with a white chinstrap; body brownish, most races darker than Canada Goose. hutchinsii palest-breasted, though greyer than the pale-breasted Canada races, with a square head and steeply sloping forehead; minima rounder-headed and smallest; leucopareia with a white neck-ring between black neck and dark brown breast. Female virtually identical, slightly lighter.
krunut1: Upperparts blue-grey, flight feathers grey-brown; black fore-crown; long white supercilium underlined by a black eyestripe that fades behind the eye; throat white, rest of the underparts dirty white to pale grey with a large rusty-red patch on the crescent-shaped breast; undertail rufous with white tips; thin white eye-ring. Female: black crown smaller and less sharply cut off behind. Bill dark horn-grey, cutting edge and lower mandible base blue-grey; iris dark cinnamon to brown; legs grey-brown to dark grey.
dalpel1: Silvery-white, greyer or creamier in winter; head and neck feathers long, soft and curled, forming a shaggy nape crest that gives an unkempt look and is longest when breeding. In flight the underwing looks almost wholly pale, with only the wingtips black. Bill grey-black, upper edge yellow, nail orange; pouch orange-red when breeding, otherwise yellow to orange; iris whitish to pale blue; legs dark to mid grey.
humwar1: Greenish above with a grey-green cast, crown browner with at most a hint of a pale central stripe; long beige supercilium not reaching far into the nape, dark eyestripe; cream-white below, washed beige on throat, cheeks, breast and flanks. One clear pale wing bar on the greater coverts, the median-covert bar a faint vestige; tertials cream to white-tipped. Sexes alike. Bill dark horn-brown, base flesh or pale horn, lower mandible dark; iris brown; legs greyish olive-brown to dark horn, sometimes orange-tinged.
moured1: Male: black head with a broad white band over the eye and down the side of the neck; upperparts black but for a large white wing patch; rump and tail chestnut; underparts rich orange-red. Female: pale brown head and upperparts, underparts paler orange than the male but redder than female Common Redstart; the wing pale where the male shows white.
citfin1: Male: face, underparts and rump yellow-green to lemon; crown, nape and neck sides ash-grey; back olive-grey to olive-green with black streaks; two yellow-green wing bars on a dark wing; tail dark. Female: duller and greyer, grey on the breast as well; young females duller below. Juvenile: brown, with no yellow or green at all.
uraowl1: Pale greyish-brown to whitish overall, back and mantle darker grey-brown with contrasting whitish markings; underparts pale cream-ochre to grey-brown, boldly streaked dark brown without crossbars. Tail rounded, evenly barred, usually five narrow pale bars and a pale tip. In flight the underwing is buffish-white with heavy dark bars along the trailing edge and tip. Northern birds palest, some nearly white. Eyes small, close-set and almond-shaped, dark brown to reddish-brown; bill orange-yellow.
blkfra: Male: black head and breast divided by a chestnut collar; large white cheek patch; flanks and breast sides spotted white, the marks U-shaped lower down; back and wings scalloped golden-brown with tawny-buff subterminal bands; tail black, barred white or grey. Female: yellow-brown, heavily vermiculated, chestnut hindneck, black throat, no cheek patch, outer tail feathers black; wings brown in both sexes. Legs reddish-brown to red, the male's with a backward-pointing spur; iris brown.
eabwar1: Plain grey-green above with a dull grey crown and mantle; rump yellow-green; upperwing and tail green-toned with blackish centres, tertials pale-edged; underwing-coverts and axillaries pale yellow; throat, breast, belly and undertail-coverts white. Sexes alike. Legs brown to pale grey-brown.
fuwduc: Head, neck and breast rich buff; back darker brown, mantle feathers buff-tipped; dark brown to black stripe down the crown centre and hind-neck to the mantle; whitish stripes on the flanks; flight feathers and tail dark brown; white crescent on the rump against the black tail. Female slightly smaller and duller; juvenile paler below and duller, especially on the flanks. Bill long and grey; legs grey.
gresni1: Mottled brown above, underparts paler and barred right across, with no clean white belly; dark stripe from the bill base through the eye. Greater and median coverts white-tipped, making two wing bars; outer tail feathers white, showing as broad white triangles at the tail sides. Juvenile: less white on the tail, wing bars more diffuse. Sexes alike, female averaging larger.
armgul1: Adult: head, breast and underparts white in summer; in winter head finely streaked brown, more heavily on neck and breast sides. Upperparts medium grey; extensive black wingtip with only small white mirrors; broad white trailing edge to the inner wing. First-winter: mainly brown with whitish rump, pale inner primaries and a narrow, sharply defined black tail band. Bill yellow, short, black band before the pale tip, red gonys spot; iris usually dark, orbital ring red; legs yellow, greener in winter.
baicra1: Crown, nape and hindneck cinnamon with diffuse black streaks; supercilium, face and foreneck light blue-grey, some birds cinnamon on ear-coverts and lores; upperparts warm ochre-brown streaked black and spotted white on mantle and coverts; belly white, flanks, thighs and undertail-coverts sharply barred black and white. Female duller brown above. Immature: duller, underparts extensively barred; chicks black. Bill green to yellow-green with a dark ridge and tip, never red at the base; iris bright red; legs and feet olive-green to yellowish olive.
hoomer: Male: head, neck, breast and upperparts black with white markings, a large white patch on each side of the crest; flanks chestnut, breast and underparts largely white with white stripes across the crop and breast. Female: grey-brown, upperparts nearly black, crest light reddish-brown. Both sexes show narrow white stripes along the tertials. First-winter: neck and upperparts grey-brown, tertial edges narrower. Iris yellow in the male, brown in females of all ages; male's eye already pale in the first winter; female's bill yellowish grey.
rinduc: Male: head glossy purple-black, breast, back and stern black, flanks grey with a white wedge at the front; belly white; cinnamon neck ring usually impossible to see. Female: grey-brown with dark brown back, pale throat, pale surround to the bill base, pale eye-ring and often a pale line back from the eye. Bill grey, white band before a black tip, white line round the base; iris yellow in the male, brown in the female.
palwar5: Dark olive-green above, whitish below, sometimes pale yellow on the breast; bold lemon-yellow supercilium reaching the nape and running into a pale forehead band, dark loral and eye-stripe, and a clear pale yellow central crown stripe on an otherwise dark crown; two prominent sulphur-yellow wing bars on median and greater coverts; pale yellow rump patch about 10 mm wide. Bill short, blackish-brown with yellowish cutting edges and lower-mandible base; iris brown; legs brown tinged green or grey.
whhduc1: Male: chalk-white head with black crown and a dark spot at the eye, body reddish-brown to grey; some individuals entirely black-headed. Female and juvenile: grey-brown body, white face, a larger dark crown patch reaching down over the eye, and an indistinct dark stripe across the cheek. Adult male's bill clearly light blue in spring, otherwise grey; female and juvenile grey-billed.
oltwar1: Pale olive-grey to grey above, whitish-grey below; obvious pale wing panel, wingtips and tail blackish, the long tail otherwise dark grey; rump pale grey-white; outer webs of the outer tail feathers almost white. Dingy white supercilium, often faint, from bill base to eye, merging with a white upper eye-ring; lower eye-ring faint or absent. No marked difference between the sexes. Bill long and strong, the lower mandible clearly orange-yellow; legs unusually stout.
combul2: Head dark brown to blackish, contrasting; upperparts brown, wings and tail grey to dark grey; underparts dull grey-brown, paler whitish on belly and vent. A small crest is sometimes raised. Sexes alike, male averaging larger. Some races show yellow undertail-coverts. Bill, legs and feet black; iris dark brown, with an indistinct dark orbital ring.
barpar2: Back grey-brown, breast grey, belly rust-buff; flanks white with rufous streaks. Throat and side of head pale grey, no white chin patch; instead a broad chestnut collar spotted white, a band down the centre of the crown and a streak back from the cheek. Supercilium pale blue-grey; a long pink stripe runs vertically behind the eye. Outer tail feathers rufous. Legs red.
sursco: Male velvety black with white patches on forehead and nape; bill orange at range, patterned white, red and yellow with a black spot near the base. Female browner and near-uniform, with indistinct pale patches on the cheek below the eye and often a whitish nape patch. Juvenile paler and browner, breast and belly whitish. Male's iris white; female's bill black with green or blue tones.
y00427: Male: head and upperparts black, broad white half-collar, large white scapular patch, white unstreaked rump, orange restricted to throat and breast. Female: upperparts and head pale brown, streaked, white neck patches but no full collar, rump pale, unstreaked pinkish-buff, throat whitish. Winter male mottled and intermediate, with a whinchat-like supercilium.
duswar: Upperparts uniformly dark grey-brown, crown concolorous; long pale supercilium over a dark eye-stripe, and a thin white eye-ring. Underparts dirty white to buff, breast a shade darker, flanks and undertail-coverts cream, vent white. Sexes alike; juveniles more olive above. Bill dark, with a little red-brown at the base; legs dark.
desfin2: Predominantly pale sandy, greyer on head, back and breast, warmer ochre on face and forehead; uppertail-coverts warm red-brown; belly and undertail-coverts whitish. Wing boldly black and white with a broad rosy-pink slash across the coverts, obvious in flight; tail black centrally, white-edged. Male: black lores, black bill, narrowly white-edged tertials. Female: duller, these parts grey-brown. Bill stout, black in the male; legs and feet dark flesh-coloured.
martea1: Pale sandy to light grey-brown, diffusely blotched off-white — cream feathers with dark grey-brown edges; underparts barred; dark eye-patch, sometimes running back to the nape; tail white. Sexes alike, the female's crest weaker and she averages smaller; juvenile similar but more heavily blotched off-white. No speculum on the secondaries. Bill long, narrow and black; breeding male with a narrow blue band behind the nail, blue bill edges and lower base of the upper mandible.
levspa1: Male: blue-grey above, head included, wingtips dark; underparts and leg feathers finely barred rufous on white, looking almost white at range; white throat split by a dark central stripe, sometimes faint. Female: slate-grey above, barred red-brown below, often showing the throat line. Juvenile: dark grey-brown above, breast coarsely streaked, flanks and underwing barred and spotted, throat stripe clear. Legs orange-yellow, cere yellow.
wallcr1: Blue-grey; flight and tail feathers darker, the tail short and black with a narrow white fringe. Coverts and the basal half of the primaries and secondaries crimson to brick-red with white spots, mostly hidden on the folded wing. Male: throat black in summer, fore-breast dark grey to black. Female: throat grey or whitish. Winter birds and juveniles white-throated. Bill long, thin, decurved and black.
whwsno1: Upperparts dull earth-brown, underparts and rump white, head grey. A long narrow white panel shows on the closed wing; in flight the wing is largely white with black primaries and alula, and the white tail carries a thin black terminal band and blackish central feathers. Summer: black throat bib, veiled by pale fringes in winter. Female slightly paler. Bill black in summer, yellow to ivory in winter; legs and iris black.
palsun2: Breeding male looks black at range; close to, metallic green above, violet-blue on the crown, steel-blue on the uppertail-coverts, blue on the throat; wings and tail black. Yellow to orange-red pectoral tufts, hard to see except at close range. Female and juvenile grey-brown above, whitish below with a faint yellow wash. Non-breeding male as female, with scattered black feathers. Bill black, thin, downcurved and pointed.
mstlar1: Greyish-brown above, dark-streaked, white below, with fine streaking across the breast and a pale supercilium. No dark neck patches. Sexes alike. Colour varies across the range and is not a reliable mark; overall browner and less rufous than its relatives.
bcbeat1: Predominantly green; crown, upperparts and wings dark, iridescent olive-green. Broad black eye-stripe from the bill base almost to the nape, white supercilium, cheeks and ear-coverts pale sky-blue, pale yellow at the bill base and on the chin, throat rust-red. Undertail-coverts pale green, tail grey below. Sexes alike, the female's streamers shorter. Bill black; legs dark; iris red-brown.
mouwar1: Crown almost black, contrasting sharply with a prominent white supercilium; ear-coverts dark grey-brown, throat paler. Back finely streaked brown, more rufous on nape and back than Sedge Warbler; underparts white. Sexes alike. Juvenile more heavily streaked, with markings on the breast.
fifser1: Male: head, nape, throat and neck black, with a glowing blood-red forehead; body heavily streaked sooty-black on yellowish, rump orange- to beige-yellow; two orange-yellow wingbars from the pale covert tips. Female: forehead patch smaller, head often sooty-grey and streaked rather than black, rump streaked. Juvenile: cinnamon-brown on forehead, face and throat, upperparts more heavily streaked. Bill short and stubby, grey to black; iris dark brown to black; legs blackish to dark brown.
sacibi2: Body white; blue-black ornamental plumes over the square tail and the closed wing. Wing tips black, forming a broad black rear border in flight. Bare red skin runs along the leading underwing and on the breast sides, deepest when breeding. Juvenile: dirty white, some feathering on the neck, greenish-brown scapulars, more black in the primary coverts. Head, neck, bill and legs black, the decurved bill greyer; iris brown with a dark red orbital ring.
desspa1: Male: crown, nape and cheeks grey; black bib edged by a pale yellow malar stripe running onto yellow neck sides; supercilium white before the eye, buff behind; back reddish-brown, heavily black-streaked; coverts rufous against a blackish wing. Female: like a paler House Sparrow, head plain pale brown with a broad supercilium behind the eye. Race yatii sandier and yellow-washed below.
grapri1: Upperparts pale grey-brown, crown and back finely dark-streaked; underparts dirty white with buff flanks. No supercilium and no eye-stripe. Each tail feather carries a black subterminal band and a white tip, showing clearly from below. Winter adults brighter sandy above, streaking weaker, more buff on the sides. Sexes similar. Bill black in the breeding male, brown in the female, paler in winter.
marwar1: Uniformly smoke-grey above and below, with no brick-red on the underparts and no white spots on the throat; throat paler than the rest. Male: darker patches on the forehead and between the eye and the bill. Female paler and duller, but likewise without a trace of brown. Juvenile grey below with a whiter throat, belly and breast centre. Bill base, iris and legs red; the juvenile's iris dark.
rekcoo1: Glossy black on head, neck and fore-body, somewhat paler behind; white frontal shield with two red knobs above it, swollen and visible only when breeding, and hard to see at any distance. Feathering between shield and bill rounded, not pointed. Secondaries with no white trailing edge. Juvenile: dark brown, throat and foreneck pale, shield barely developed. Bill white with a blue-grey tinge; iris red; legs yellow-grey to yellow-green, toes blue-grey. Juvenile: bill yellow-orange, legs orange-red, eyes black.
crwfin2: Male: broad dark, almost black crown on an ochre-to-sand head; dark rose lores and cheeks; supercilium, ear-coverts and neck sides paler beige; throat and breast sandy-brown, dark-streaked, heaviest on the breast; pink-white wing panels, pink rump, white belly. Female: crown brownish, heavily mixed with paler feathers. Bill horn-yellow, heavy and conical; legs pale brown, feet darker.
comcan: Male: head and underparts yellow-green, forehead, face and supercilium yellower; ear patch framed by a dark malar stripe; upperparts grey-green with dark streaks, rump dull yellow; lower belly and undertail-coverts whitish; dark streaks along the sides. Female: duller, head and breast greyer. Juvenile: largely brown, dark-streaked. Upper mandible flesh to pale lead-grey, blackish towards the tip, lower horn-coloured; iris grey-black; legs and toes grey-brown.
houbun3: Male: head grey with lengthwise black-and-white streaking, eye- and malar stripes weak; breast grey and spotted, cut off sharply from the throat; back rust-brown and unstreaked; belly and wings cinnamon-rufous; no white in the tail. Female: grey of the head tinged brown, streaking more diffuse, colours paler throughout. Lower mandible yellow.
piekin1: Black and white throughout; black mask through the eye under a white supercilium; upperparts barred black. Male: two black breast bands, the second narrow. Female: a single, often broken band. Race travancoreensis darker with less white; insignis much bigger-billed.
mouwhe2: Black and white: white crown, nape, breast and belly against a black face, throat and back; wings look wholly black at rest but show white flight-feather bases as a white flag in flight; tail mostly white with an even black terminal band and a central black intrusion forming an inverted T. Nominate rufous-vented. Female only subtly duller.
steeag1: Uniform dark brown, adults with darker centres to the greater coverts and, mainly in the east, pale rufous to orange-yellow patches on nape and hindcrown; wingtips blackish, tail blackish and unbarred; often a pale beige band across the lower secondaries; throat pale. Massive gape-line running back level with the rear of the eye, longer than in any other Aquila; eyes deep-set; nostril oval.
chiwig1: Male: forehead and face below the eye white, rest of the head black glossed green or purple, white ear-patch; neck and hindcrown black; breast barred black and white; back grey-black with sharply contrasting white feather tips, uppertail-coverts white; belly white; flanks and undertail-coverts chestnut. Female: duller, flanks paler brown, head without gloss. Juvenile: rust on the flanks reduced or absent. Bill blue-grey with a black tip; legs and feet grey; iris dark brown.
mouchi2: Brown above, cream-white below, flanks buff to dull yellow; race lorenzii warmer and darker brown than the nominate. Bill fine and dark; feet black.
grnwar1: Moss-green above, whitish below, with pale yellow cheeks, throat and forebreast and a clear yellow supercilium running to the bill base; one strong pale wing bar and often a short, fainter second, best marked on young birds. Lower mandible pale orange.
ricpip1: Brown above with dark streaking, pale below; breast streaked, belly plain; throat and flanks warm buff to rusty, the throat clearly streaked; face strongly marked with pale lores and supercilium, dark eyestripe, moustachial and malar stripes; two pale wing-bars; outer tail feathers white. Legs long and yellow-brown; bill long and dark with a yellowish base to the lower mandible.
lanwar: Dull brown above with black streaking, whitish-grey below with small lance-head streaks that carry onto the undertail-coverts; dark marks sharply defined though variable; near-black tertials with even, sharply edged pale fringes. Sexes alike; juvenile yellower below.
delpri1: Grey-brown above with broad dark streaks and generally dark-toned; head plain, without eyestripe or supercilium; underparts pale with clear marks on the breast sides; each rounded tail feather black-and-white tipped, obvious from below; upper tail strongly barred. Race akyildizi darkest and most heavily streaked, with the brightest buff flanks.
rosgoo: Pure white but for the black flight feathers; adults with all-white secondaries, juveniles dark-centred. Juvenile: largely grey, paler and sometimes yellowish on the belly, flight feathers brownish. A dark morph occurs but is extremely rare. Bill pink, the bluish base carrying warty growths that increase with age, weaker on females; no dark lips; eyes dark brown; legs deep pink.
corfin1: Male: face and underparts yellow, back rust-brown with dark streaks, two yellow-green bars across the dark wing, uppertail-coverts grey rather than olive; markings diffuse overall. Female: duller.
chifla1: Pink throughout, the depth of colour depending on diet; chicks grey or peach, gaining pink as they age. More than half the bill black, the base much paler; legs grey to beige-grey with strikingly red intertarsal joints and feet, the diagnostic mark.
cypwar1: Male: black hood, grey back, white malar streaks, and the whole underside coarsely spotted black; flanks grey-beige; undertail-coverts dark-centred; tertials, secondaries and greater coverts broadly white-edged. Female: head grey, back grey-brown, spotting confined to throat and breast, underparts whitish. Eye-ring thin and white; bill base yellow-pink.
blwpra1: Dark olive-brown above, head and back brown, flight feathers black; chin and throat cream, ringed by a black band against the grey-brown breast; belly white, rump white; underwing-coverts wholly black. Juvenile: throat band absent, mantle feathers with large cream tips. Bill short and black with a red base; no eye-ring.
atlfly1: Male: coal-black above with large white patches on both forehead and wing, and an all-black tail. Female: tail blacker above than in its close relatives, rump pale grey.
gbhgul2: Summer adult: black hood with narrow white crescents above and below the eye; back and upperwing pale grey; primaries silvery white with conspicuous white mirrors and a narrow black subterminal band; body and tail otherwise white. Winter: hood reduced to a dark eye-mask with dusky crown and hindneck. Juvenile: brown-scaled back and coverts, brown breast-sides, sharp black tail band. Bill tricoloured: dark yellow base, narrow black then red bands, yellow tip, the red band lost in winter; iris dark; legs yellow.
rudduc: Breeding male: blackish cap over bright white cheeks, body rich chestnut. Non-breeding male: dull grey-brown above, paler below, crown blackish-grey, white cheeks and white undertail-coverts kept. Female and first-year male brownish like the winter male but with a blurry stripe across the pale cheek patch. South American birds: males wholly black-headed. Male's bill bright light blue in summer, dull dark grey in winter; female's bill darker.
swagoo1: Upperparts greyish-brown with thin pale fringes to the larger feathers; crown and hindneck maroon, sharply cut against the pale buff foreneck and lower head; thin white stripe round the bill base; underside pale buff, darker streaks on belly and flanks; upper- and undertail-coverts white; wings dark and unpatterned in flight. Juvenile: duller. Bill wholly black — unique in the genus; legs and feet orange; irides maroon.
yecbis: Breeding male: forehead, crown, hindcrown and nape brilliant golden-yellow, hindneck feathers black-tipped; head-sides, chin, throat and belly black, with a broad black collar on the hindneck; yellow shoulder patch, lower back and rump yellow; wings and tail brown. Female and non-breeding male: pale brown above with dark streaking, pale supercilium, off-white below, finely streaked on breast and flanks. Breeding male's bill black, otherwise horn as in the female; legs and feet pinkish brown; iris brown.
lobdow: Whitish supercilium, dark loral stripe running past the eye. Breeding: crown dark, neck, breast and belly rufous, breast barred black, flanks barred white. Non-breeding: drab grey, upperparts and breast darker, belly white. Tail barred black and white, black bars near twice the white's width; white wedge up the back to mid-mantle. Juvenile: as breeding adult, paler. Bill dark, sometimes paler at the base; legs and feet pale olive to yellow-olive; iris dark brown.
commyn: Body chestnut-brown; head and breast black and slightly glossy, forming a hood; large white patches on both surfaces of the wing contrasting with black primaries; undertail-coverts white to pale grey; tail brown shading to black with a white tip. Sexes alike. Juvenile: duller and darker, the black parts without gloss. Bill and stout legs bright yellow; bare yellow patch of skin behind the eye.
namdov1: Male: forehead, face, throat and breast black, sharply cut from pale blue-grey head-sides; nape, back and inner coverts very pale brown, belly white; coverts pale grey with black- to red-glossed spots; rump grey-brown with a white, black-edged bar; chestnut primaries flash in flight. Female: no black mask, forecrown and breast dull grey-brown. Juvenile: dark blotched on wings and shoulders. Male's bill long, orange-red paling to yellow at the tip; female's duller, grey with a red base; iris dark brown, eye-ring grey.
levwoo1: Dark moss-green above, yellowish-green below; nape crimson; rump chrome yellow, brighter than the green woodpecker's; outer webs of the primaries barred black and white, outer tail feathers barred grey-green and white; flanks and lower belly with olive-grey arrowheads. Black moustache pale-bordered above. Male: crown crimson. Female: crown grey, wholly without red. Lores and eye-surround never black. Bill slate grey, pale at the base and grey at the tip, slightly shorter than the green woodpecker's; feet slate grey.
whrswi1: Very dark blackish-brown throughout; clean-cut white throat patch standing out sharply; narrow but distinct white band across the rump, seen in flight mainly from the side; diffusely paler tips to the secondaries. Sexes alike.
deswhe1: Male: crown, nape and mantle warm sandy-grey; rump pale buff to white; tail almost wholly black, white only at the extreme base-sides; chin, throat, lores and ear-coverts black; supercilium and scapulars white; breast sandy-buff, belly creamy-white. Female: rump sandier, lores, chin and throat pale buff, tail's dark brownish-black. First-winter male and female drab pale grey-brown. Juvenile: upperparts pale-centred, brown-tipped, speckled.
lesyel: Breeding: upperparts mottled grey-brown, black and white; head pale grey-white finely streaked; supercilium diffuse, white eye-ring and white chin clear; breast streaked and spotted dark brown, flanks finely barred; underparts white. Non-breeding: upperparts uniform grey-brown, breast streaked only. Juvenile: throat paler, upperparts browner, breast greyer. Legs bright yellow; bill black, in many birds yellowish-brown at the base; iris dark brown.
tstlar1: Crown finely streaked blackish, crest raisable; upperparts dark red-brown to brown with broader dark streaks that fade towards the tail; median coverts darker than the rest of the wing; supercilium narrow and whitish, never bold; underparts white, breast finely streaked and, with the flanks, washed red-brown to cinnamon. Sexes alike. Juvenile: somewhat spotted below. Bill horn-grey, darker on the culmen, base of the lower mandible yellowish; legs brownish to yellow-brown.
upcwar1: Pale grey-brown: crown and mantle light brownish-grey, rump and tail-coverts sandy-ochre, underparts dirty white. Grey-white supercilium from bill base to behind the eye, merging with a thin eye-ring; lores darker grey; ear-coverts grey-brown. Tail brown-grey at the base, blackening towards the tip, outer feathers narrowly white-fringed; pale streak on the wing; tail and wing-tips darker than body. Sexes alike. Bill blackish or dark grey-horn above, pale yellow or pink below; iris dark brown, often faintly reddish.
padwar1: Broad, evenly wide, long pale supercilium, white in breeding adults and often edged darker above and below. Upperparts unstreaked: warm orange-brown to rufous when fresh, dull olive-brown when worn, nape paler; rump warm rusty buff, always contrasting with the mantle. Throat whitish, breast-sides, flanks and underparts warm yellowish-buff. Sexes alike. Juvenile: richer buff below. Bill straw-yellow with a dark tip and dark upper mandible; iris pale red-brown in adults, dark in young birds; legs pink to dark grey-brown.
brnrav1: Head and throat distinctly brownish-black, giving the name; rest of the plumage black glossed purple, blue or purplish-blue, with a bronze-brown tone on the nape that shows only at close range. Feathers fade fast, so birds can look plainly brown by the time they moult. Bill, legs and feet black; toes often yellow, especially in the Middle East.
palroc1: Pale beige-grey throughout and wholly unstreaked; short, faint pale supercilium; two indistinct paler wing-bars; white spots at the tip of the tail, showing in flight. Bill dark grey when breeding, paler beige-grey in winter.
ortdov: Upper back, head, neck and breast dark brown-pink; rump blue-grey; belly and undertail-coverts whitish grey. Scapulars, tertials and inner coverts black-centred with broad rust-brown fringes, giving a scaly look; median and greater coverts white-tipped, forming two clear pale wing-bars; primaries black. Neck-side patch of fine parallel black stripes on blue-grey. Sexes alike. Legs red, bill dark grey; no bare patch of skin round the eye.
duplar1: Cryptically marked in brown; thin pale crown stripe, pale eye-stripe, dark-streaked breast, white outer tail feathers, and no white trailing edge to the wing. North-western birds mainly brown-grey above and pale below; south-eastern birds rufous above. Sexes alike. Race margaritae longer-billed and more rufous.
radacc2: Dark cheeks and dark crown set off a broad dirty-white supercilium; upperparts cold brown; underparts warm beige, the orange tone concentrated on the breast.
trufin2: Summer male: head and neck grey, upper back pale brown; breast, belly, rump and tail pink, the tail dark at edges and centre; pink flush also over forecrown, back and wing-coverts. Otherwise plain sandy and unmarked — greyish head-sides, caramel neck and breast, dark ochre wings and tail. Winter male, female and juvenile far paler and less contrasted, juveniles browner. Male's bill vivid orange to deep red when breeding, pale orange or horn otherwise and in females, yellowish-brown in juveniles; dark eye, faint pale ring.
snoowl1: Mostly white — purer than a polar bear or Arctic fox. Adult male nearly plain white, at most a few dark spots on head, ear-tufts and some primary and secondary tips. Female far more spotted, barred dark brown on crown and underparts, flight and tail feathers faintly barred. Young male as an adult female; young female densely dark-barred throughout. Eyes large and bright golden-yellow; bill black, largely hidden under dense fine white bristles.
diadov1: Male: head, neck and breast pale blue-grey; upperwing-coverts fawn-brown with fine round white spots edged black; mantle and tail grey-brown; belly and undertail-coverts creamy. Central four tail feathers grey-brown, dark-tipped, outer ones white at the base. Female: duller, more brown on hindneck and mantle. Juvenile: no white wing spots, breast grey. Bill dark grey; iris orange-red; bare eye-ring bright red, browner in female; legs and feet pink. Juvenile: bill pale grey, eye-ring fawn, legs grey-black.
465888: Sexes alike. Upperparts light brown, paler on the lower back; throat, upper breast and underwing-coverts pale grey, rest of underparts dirty white; no breast band. Short square tail with small white patches near the tips of all but the central and outermost feather pairs. Juvenile: pale buff to rufous fringes above, washed rufous throat and vent. Iris brown; small bill mainly black; legs brownish-pink.
